contracts.changeImpact: An accepted change alters stored metadata or its later consumer input. Read the response and observe the relevant controller; schema or metadata acceptance alone does not prove reconciliation.
crossFieldConditions: These JSON cases decode a fresh ObjectMeta with its immediate parent present. Missing ancestors prevent child decoding. They do not define JSON merge-patch null deletion or apply omission; those operations merge before validation and ownership processing.

REST create decodes and defaults, wipes client system metadata, runs ownership/admission and enters the store. The store sets UID/creation time and generated name, then BeforeCreate enforces scope and strategy/common validation before storage. A validation failure establishes no stored object.

Replacement update uses the current storage object, checks resourceVersion, restores generation before strategy preparation, fills an omitted UID and preserves lifecycle values before common/resource validation. A stale nonempty version returns Conflict; fetch again and recompute the intended change.

Labels and annotations are ordinary readable resource metadata, not Secret storage. Do not place bearer tokens, passwords or private keys here; use the authorized Secret reference appropriate to the consumer and redact metadata when collecting diagnostics.

Authentication, authorization, admission mutation, storage failures and actual controller configuration remain independent boundaries. On an uncertain create response, read by returned/intended identity before retry; generateName retry can create another object if the first call committed.

The CRD strategy sets generation 1 on create. On update it preserves configured status first and increments generation if content other than metadata changes. Metadata-only label/annotation/finalizer changes do not increment it.

The pinned Argo CRDs do not declare a status subresource. Status remains ordinary schema data, written with whole-resource patches; the CRD status reset route described separately is not an installed Argo status endpoint. Non-metadata status changes can therefore increment generation.

Full CRD create/replacement bodies decode implicit metadata into ObjectMeta and convert it back to unstructured. ObjectMeta managedFields is omitempty: [] has zero length and is omitted, so it becomes absent before field management; [{}] has one item and survives. Patch transformations require their own path analysis; these complete-body outcomes do not prove every patch format.

Incoming CRD request decoding does not enable malformed-metadata dropping or generation repair. Storage codec decoding enables both for persisted objects. A stored-object repair branch cannot be used to promise acceptance of malformed incoming ObjectMeta.
Argo CD v3.5.2 uses k8s.io/apimachinery v0.36.1; the server operation expectations here are Kubernetes v1.35.0 source, not that client dependency.

The Argo CRD envelopes and opaque metadata inventory remain the pinned chart schema authority. The Kubernetes ObjectMeta reference is a receiving obligation independent of that opacity; it does not add schema properties.

Argo event-label construction uses Application labels first and fills absent keys from its resolved AppProject. A present empty Application label still wins over the project value. Include-key patterns select labels, then exclude-key patterns remove them. Project lookup failure logs a warning and keeps the Application labels. These event labels do not change Kubernetes admission or select application target resources.

Application name/namespace forms QualifiedName for queues, InstanceName for resource/cache identity and RBACName together with its selected project. AppProject access and allowed Application namespaces remain separate from Kubernetes resource authorization.

The Application informer queues namespace/name keys for add, update and delete events after canProcessApp permits the object. Updates request refresh by QualifiedName; an equal resourceVersion can add configured jitter. Queueing and cache identity do not establish a successful reconciliation. Kubernetes client operations and Argo namespace/project authorization must still permit the selected object.

For an Application generated by ApplicationSet, its controller reads the current object and prepares the desired metadata. Configured preserved label and annotation keys keep their existing values, including empty strings; the callback then replaces the label and annotation maps with the prepared maps. IgnoreApplicationDifferences can remove changes from the patch. Equal results skip a write; read, preparation and patch errors do not establish persistence.

The ApplicationSet child-event comparison checks spec, labels, annotations and finalizers, treating nil and empty maps/lists as equal. Resource-version or generation changes alone do not trigger this comparison. Progressive-sync mode separately checks selected health, sync and operation-state observations. This event filter is distinct from admission and successful reconciliation.

ApplicationSet preserves existing pre-delete and post-delete finalizer prefixes, including staged suffixes, when preparing an Application. This preservation does not apply to every token. For an obsolete Application with an invalid destination, its deletion helper removes only the exact foreground resources finalizer before DELETE; background and other tokens are retained. A removed token does not establish target cleanup.

ApplicationSet indexes an Application by the name of a controller reference with its expected group/version and kind, then lists that name within the ApplicationSet namespace. The named index/query does not compare owner UID. When the ApplicationSet is deleting and its effective policy disallows deletion, the selected helper clears the entire ownerReferences list on each returned Application and updates it; a list or update error stops that helper. Inspect the actual owner UID and returned objects before relying on preservation or repeating an interrupted change.

ApplicationSet RollingSync uses generated Application labels to select rollout steps. A missing key with operator In excludes the Application from that step. One Application can match more than one step; this code warns about repeated selection. This consumer is separate from Kubernetes Pod selectors and requires the ApplicationSet strategy and controller.

The Argo Application updateApp helper merges new labels/annotations into the stored maps when its merge argument is true; otherwise it replaces those maps with the new maps. This server operation is distinct from a direct Kubernetes full replacement or patch. Inspect the chosen server request before assuming that an omitted key is retained.

The hydrate annotation requests hydration for any present value, with exact hard selecting hard hydration. Hydration status persistence consumes the annotation. Application summary includes link-prefix annotation values as external links; that collection code does not validate the values as URLs. The separate managed-by-url validator skips missing/empty values and reports InvalidSpecError for an invalid external URL. These consumer rules do not replace general annotation syntax or byte limits.

Application manifest-generate-paths is forwarded to manifest generation. With a prior synced revision, repository depth zero and a nonempty annotation, this controller requests path-specific revision updating. An empty value does not select that optimization; repository failures still return errors.

The manifest-generate-paths consumer splits a nonempty annotation on semicolons, trims whitespace and skips empty entries. On the Linux repository server, a leading slash selects a repository-root path; a relative entry is joined to the source path and cleaned. A configured hydration sync source instead selects its own source path and ignores this annotation. These paths select refresh work, not access authorization.

Webhook refresh also requires a matching repository URL and changed source revision. When either the changed-file list or selected path list is empty, the path matcher requires refresh. Otherwise it tests exact paths, descendants and filepath patterns. A match queues refresh, with optional jitter; it does not prove completed generation, synchronization or hydration. An unmatched change can still update manifest-cache revision keys when cache warming is enabled.

argocd.argoproj.io/refresh requests normal refresh for any present value except exact hard, which selects hard refresh. Absence does not request refresh; empty/unknown values still request normal refresh. Reconciliation persistence removes this key after the refresh. The skip-reconcile annotation uses ParseBool: true stops processing, false continues and invalid/empty text logs then continues.

Deletion confirmation uses the deletion-approved annotation timestamp: missing, empty or invalid RFC3339 does not approve; a valid timestamp at or after deletion start approves. This does not waive Kubernetes admission or target cleanup.

Application resource finalizers select controller cleanup, separate from the API GC finalizers. The controller rereads the Application, resolves project/target access, runs pre-delete hooks, waits for deletion confirmation/pending live deletion, deletes permitted resources with selected foreground/background policy, rereads remaining resources and only then removes its cascade token. Post-delete hooks retain their own tokens while incomplete.

If destination-cluster lookup fails, this pinned Argo branch removes cascade/pre/post-delete tokens and returns after updating finalizers; it does not prove target resources were cleaned up. Other target access, hook, list or delete errors can retain tokens. Recovery must inspect Application and target state before repeating destructive work.

continuousApplications removes any stale immutable-bundle-path annotation and writes the selected path only for a unique releases/gitops/<bundle>/{buster,nova,prism} directory with resources.yaml. The platform health Lua uses that equality only when a successful applied operation has another revision than the currently compared main revision. Healthy/synced state, successful operation and matching applied repoURL/path/targetRevision/directory include remain required. The marker affects reported health, not synchronization, ownership or content immutability.

KubeClaw GitOps bootstrap derives a root name from the first runtime namespace and a separate workload project name. Bootstrap Applications and AppProjects carry kubeclaw.dev/gitops-root. Preflight reads existing objects by name in the selected Argo namespace and rejects a different root label. Its bootstrap-Application exemption also requires matching name, namespace and spec.project. A matching label alone grants neither Kubernetes nor Argo permission. The chart emits kubeclaw.dev/gitops-project on group Applications; spec.project remains the actual Argo project selector.

KubeClaw authors argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave=-1 on bootstrap AppProjects and the supported GitOps chart copies each group wave to its Application. The parent sync engine parses the annotation with Atoi and orders by phase before wave, then kind and name. Missing or invalid wave text falls back to Helm hook weight, then zero when that weight is absent or invalid. A wave orders the parent resource tasks; it does not directly synchronize the child workload or bypass its project and health checks.

The maintained SPIRE Application selects compare-options=ServerSideDiff=true. Argo splits the annotation on commas, trims entries, ignores empty entries and matches exact options. ServerSideDiff=true enables server-side comparison unless ServerSideDiff=false is also present, which takes precedence. Omission leaves the controller setting in effect. A successful dry-run comparison does not persist the target or establish synchronization.

Platform child Applications carry ignore-healthcheck=true and kubeclaw.io/health-mode=observed. Only the exact string true makes the parent health aggregator skip that live child; this does not stop the child controller or make it healthy. The installed KubeClaw Lua health customization first reports selected comparison/sync errors and failed operations as Degraded. After those checks, exact observed reports stored child health without requiring synchronization to its selected revision. Other values use the strict source/revision/destination/operation checks. The customization must be installed in the actual Argo configuration.

The bootstrap runtime-namespaces annotation is a JSON array of valid GitOps namespace names. claimedNamespaces parses it and combines it with spec.destination.namespace; absent annotation contributes no extra namespace. Invalid JSON or a non-array/invalid name fails the ownership check. Bootstrap preflight requires the stored annotation text to match the newly generated claim and rejects a changed repository or namespace claim. The group chart serializes helm-releases for release context; the prerequisite check reads the bundle group helmReleases rather than trusting that annotation. Neither annotation transfers ownership or removes retained resources.

InstanceName, QualifiedName and RBACName derive identities from metadata name/namespace; GetAnnotation returns an empty string for an absent key.

RollingSync step matching tests generated Application labels and records selected Application names.

IsHydrateRequested treats every present hydrate annotation as a request and only exact hard as hard hydration.
PersistHydrationStatus removes the hydrate annotation while persisting hydration status.
Application summary collects link-prefix annotation values into a unique sorted URL list.
ValidateManagedByURL skips missing/empty values and reports InvalidSpecError when external-URL validation fails.
Manifest generation forwards the Application manifest-generate-paths annotation to the repository request.
A nonempty manifest-generate-paths annotation with a synced revision and zero repository depth selects path-specific revision updating.
Source refresh paths give a hydration sync source precedence, then split and trim annotation paths, discard empty entries and resolve root-relative or source-relative paths.
An empty changed-file or refresh-path list returns true; otherwise exact, descendant or filepath-pattern matching selects changed files.
Matching revision/repository sources use the path matcher, queue refresh with optional jitter, and otherwise can warm manifest-cache revision keys.
Application annotation constants define refresh/hydrate and manifest-generation paths.

needRefreshAppStatus gives an explicit refresh request precedence over expiry and source/destination changes.
persistReconciliationStatus removes the refresh annotation while persisting updated status.

Application finalization rereads current state; missing destination cluster removes cascade and pre/post-delete tokens, while REST-config errors return.
Pre-delete hooks retain their finalizer until complete, then the controller patches its removal.

Post-delete hooks retain their token while pending and remove it only after completion.
updateFinalizers merge-patches the Application metadata finalizers through its namespaced client.
Argo delete requires Application delete RBAC, calculates propagation finalizers and avoids adding a token after deletion starts.
The continuous producer removes stale provenance before authoring the exact qualifying immutable release path.
The health exception requires the exact marker and matching applied source; it does not treat the annotation as an execution receipt.
Bootstrap derives root/project identities and authors root labels and runtime namespace annotation.
Bootstrap ownership exemption checks identity, root label and project; other namespace claimants must match selected groups.
Preflight retrieves existing named Argo objects and rejects root-label conflicts or changed root repository/namespace claims.
The supported chart authors workload project identity, root label and project sync wave.
Each release-group Application has group identity, sync-wave/Helm-release annotations and a project label; spec.project selects its project.
The maintained platform bootstrap selects project sync wave -1.
The supported template selects group wave and serializes Helm releases as a JSON annotation.
Wave parses the annotation as an integer and falls back to Helm hook weight.
Hook weight parses its own integer annotation and otherwise returns zero.
Sync task ordering compares phase, wave, then kind before name.
The maintained SPIRE Application explicitly selects ServerSideDiff and platform health annotations.
Annotation options split comma-separated text, trim and deduplicate nonempty entries, then compare exact strings.

Parent health aggregation skips a live resource only for the exact ignore-healthcheck value true.

Namespace claims parse the runtime namespace JSON annotation, validate its array/name contract and include the destination namespace.

The hydrate annotation requests hydration for any present value, with exact hard selecting hard hydration. Hydration status persistence consumes the annotation. Application manifest-generate-paths is forwarded to manifest generation. An empty value does not select that optimization; repository failures still return errors.

The manifest-generate-paths consumer splits a nonempty annotation on semicolons, trims whitespace and skips empty entries. On the Linux repository server, a leading slash selects a repository-root path; a relative entry is joined to the source path and cleaned. A configured hydration sync source instead selects its own source path and ignores this annotation. These paths select refresh work, not access authorization.

Webhook refresh also requires a matching repository URL and changed source revision. When either the changed-file list or selected path list is empty, the path matcher requires refresh. argocd.argoproj.io/refresh requests normal refresh for any present value except exact hard, which selects hard refresh. Absence does not request refresh; empty/unknown values still request normal refresh. Reconciliation persistence removes this key after the refresh. The skip-reconcile annotation uses ParseBool: true stops processing, false continues and invalid/empty text logs then continues.

Deletion confirmation uses the deletion-approved annotation timestamp: missing, empty or invalid RFC3339 does not approve; a valid timestamp at or after deletion start approves. This does not waive Kubernetes admission or target cleanup.

continuousApplications removes any stale immutable-bundle-path annotation and writes the selected path only for a unique releases/gitops/<bundle>/{buster,nova,prism} directory with resources.yaml. The platform health Lua uses that equality only when a successful applied operation has another revision than the currently compared main revision. Healthy/synced state, successful operation and matching applied repoURL/path/targetRevision/directory include remain required. The marker affects reported health, not synchronization, ownership or content immutability.

KubeClaw authors argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave=-1 on bootstrap AppProjects and the supported GitOps chart copies each group wave to its Application. The parent sync engine parses the annotation with Atoi and orders by phase before wave, then kind and name. Missing or invalid wave text falls back to Helm hook weight, then zero when that weight is absent or invalid. A wave orders the parent resource tasks; it does not directly synchronize the child workload or bypass its project and health checks.

The maintained SPIRE Application selects compare-options=ServerSideDiff=true. Argo splits the annotation on commas, trims entries, ignores empty entries and matches exact options. ServerSideDiff=true enables server-side comparison unless ServerSideDiff=false is also present, which takes precedence. Omission leaves the controller setting in effect. A successful dry-run comparison does not persist the target or establish synchronization.

Bootstrap preflight requires the stored annotation text to match the newly generated claim and rejects a changed repository or namespace claim. The group chart serializes helm-releases for release context; the prerequisite check reads the bundle group helmReleases rather than trusting that annotation. Neither annotation transfers ownership or removes retained resources.

REST create decodes and defaults, wipes client system metadata, runs ownership/admission and enters the store. The store sets UID/creation time and generated name, then BeforeCreate enforces scope and strategy/common validation before storage. A validation failure establishes no stored object.

Replacement update uses the current storage object, checks resourceVersion, restores generation before strategy preparation, fills an omitted UID and preserves lifecycle values before common/resource validation. A stale nonempty version returns Conflict; fetch again and recompute the intended change.

Labels and annotations are ordinary readable resource metadata, not Secret storage. Do not place bearer tokens, passwords or private keys here; use the authorized Secret reference appropriate to the consumer and redact metadata when collecting diagnostics.

Authentication, authorization, admission mutation, storage failures and actual controller configuration remain independent boundaries. On an uncertain create response, read by returned/intended identity before retry; generateName retry can create another object if the first call committed.

The CRD strategy sets generation 1 on create. On update it preserves configured status first and increments generation if content other than metadata changes. Metadata-only label/annotation/finalizer changes do not increment it.

The pinned Argo CRDs do not declare a status subresource. Status remains ordinary schema data, written with whole-resource patches; the CRD status reset route described separately is not an installed Argo status endpoint. Non-metadata status changes can therefore increment generation.

Full CRD create/replacement bodies decode implicit metadata into ObjectMeta and convert it back to unstructured. ObjectMeta managedFields is omitempty: [] has zero length and is omitted, so it becomes absent before field management; [{}] has one item and survives. Patch transformations require their own path analysis; these complete-body outcomes do not prove every patch format.

Incoming CRD request decoding does not enable malformed-metadata dropping or generation repair. Storage codec decoding enables both for persisted objects. A stored-object repair branch cannot be used to promise acceptance of malformed incoming ObjectMeta.
Argo CD v3.5.2 uses k8s.io/apimachinery v0.36.1; the server operation expectations here are Kubernetes v1.35.0 source, not that client dependency.

The Argo CRD envelopes and opaque metadata inventory remain the pinned chart schema authority. The Kubernetes ObjectMeta reference is a receiving obligation independent of that opacity; it does not add schema properties.

Application name/namespace forms QualifiedName for queues, InstanceName for resource/cache identity and RBACName together with its selected project. AppProject access and allowed Application namespaces remain separate from Kubernetes resource authorization.

For an Application generated by ApplicationSet, its controller reads the current object and prepares the desired metadata. Configured preserved label and annotation keys keep their existing values, including empty strings; the callback then replaces the label and annotation maps with the prepared maps. IgnoreApplicationDifferences can remove changes from the patch. Equal results skip a write; read, preparation and patch errors do not establish persistence.

The ApplicationSet child-event comparison checks spec, labels, annotations and finalizers, treating nil and empty maps/lists as equal. Resource-version or generation changes alone do not trigger this comparison. Progressive-sync mode separately checks selected health, sync and operation-state observations. This event filter is distinct from admission and successful reconciliation.

The Argo Application updateApp helper merges new labels/annotations into the stored maps when its merge argument is true; otherwise it replaces those maps with the new maps. This server operation is distinct from a direct Kubernetes full replacement or patch. Inspect the chosen server request before assuming that an omitted key is retained.

The hydrate annotation requests hydration for any present value, with exact hard selecting hard hydration. Hydration status persistence consumes the annotation. Application summary includes link-prefix annotation values as external links; that collection code does not validate the values as URLs. The separate managed-by-url validator skips missing/empty values and reports InvalidSpecError for an invalid external URL. These consumer rules do not replace general annotation syntax or byte limits.

Application manifest-generate-paths is forwarded to manifest generation. With a prior synced revision, repository depth zero and a nonempty annotation, this controller requests path-specific revision updating. An empty value does not select that optimization; repository failures still return errors.

The manifest-generate-paths consumer splits a nonempty annotation on semicolons, trims whitespace and skips empty entries. On the Linux repository server, a leading slash selects a repository-root path; a relative entry is joined to the source path and cleaned. A configured hydration sync source instead selects its own source path and ignores this annotation. These paths select refresh work, not access authorization.

Webhook refresh also requires a matching repository URL and changed source revision. When either the changed-file list or selected path list is empty, the path matcher requires refresh. Otherwise it tests exact paths, descendants and filepath patterns. A match queues refresh, with optional jitter; it does not prove completed generation, synchronization or hydration. An unmatched change can still update manifest-cache revision keys when cache warming is enabled.

argocd.argoproj.io/refresh requests normal refresh for any present value except exact hard, which selects hard refresh. Absence does not request refresh; empty/unknown values still request normal refresh. Reconciliation persistence removes this key after the refresh. The skip-reconcile annotation uses ParseBool: true stops processing, false continues and invalid/empty text logs then continues.

Deletion confirmation uses the deletion-approved annotation timestamp: missing, empty or invalid RFC3339 does not approve; a valid timestamp at or after deletion start approves. This does not waive Kubernetes admission or target cleanup.

continuousApplications removes any stale immutable-bundle-path annotation and writes the selected path only for a unique releases/gitops/<bundle>/{buster,nova,prism} directory with resources.yaml. The platform health Lua uses that equality only when a successful applied operation has another revision than the currently compared main revision. Healthy/synced state, successful operation and matching applied repoURL/path/targetRevision/directory include remain required. The marker affects reported health, not synchronization, ownership or content immutability.

KubeClaw authors argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave=-1 on bootstrap AppProjects and the supported GitOps chart copies each group wave to its Application. The parent sync engine parses the annotation with Atoi and orders by phase before wave, then kind and name. Missing or invalid wave text falls back to Helm hook weight, then zero when that weight is absent or invalid. A wave orders the parent resource tasks; it does not directly synchronize the child workload or bypass its project and health checks.

The maintained SPIRE Application selects compare-options=ServerSideDiff=true. Argo splits the annotation on commas, trims entries, ignores empty entries and matches exact options. ServerSideDiff=true enables server-side comparison unless ServerSideDiff=false is also present, which takes precedence. Omission leaves the controller setting in effect. A successful dry-run comparison does not persist the target or establish synchronization.

Platform child Applications carry ignore-healthcheck=true and kubeclaw.io/health-mode=observed. Only the exact string true makes the parent health aggregator skip that live child; this does not stop the child controller or make it healthy. The installed KubeClaw Lua health customization first reports selected comparison/sync errors and failed operations as Degraded. After those checks, exact observed reports stored child health without requiring synchronization to its selected revision. Other values use the strict source/revision/destination/operation checks. The customization must be installed in the actual Argo configuration.

The bootstrap runtime-namespaces annotation is a JSON array of valid GitOps namespace names. claimedNamespaces parses it and combines it with spec.destination.namespace; absent annotation contributes no extra namespace. Invalid JSON or a non-array/invalid name fails the ownership check. Bootstrap preflight requires the stored annotation text to match the newly generated claim and rejects a changed repository or namespace claim. The group chart serializes helm-releases for release context; the prerequisite check reads the bundle group helmReleases rather than trusting that annotation. Neither annotation transfers ownership or removes retained resources.

REST create decodes and defaults, wipes client system metadata, runs ownership/admission and enters the store. The store sets UID/creation time and generated name, then BeforeCreate enforces scope and strategy/common validation before storage. A validation failure establishes no stored object.

Replacement update uses the current storage object, checks resourceVersion, restores generation before strategy preparation, fills an omitted UID and preserves lifecycle values before common/resource validation. A stale nonempty version returns Conflict; fetch again and recompute the intended change.

Labels and annotations are ordinary readable resource metadata, not Secret storage. Do not place bearer tokens, passwords or private keys here; use the authorized Secret reference appropriate to the consumer and redact metadata when collecting diagnostics.

Authentication, authorization, admission mutation, storage failures and actual controller configuration remain independent boundaries. On an uncertain create response, read by returned/intended identity before retry; generateName retry can create another object if the first call committed.

The CRD strategy sets generation 1 on create. On update it preserves configured status first and increments generation if content other than metadata changes. Metadata-only label/annotation/finalizer changes do not increment it.

The pinned Argo CRDs do not declare a status subresource. Status remains ordinary schema data, written with whole-resource patches; the CRD status reset route described separately is not an installed Argo status endpoint. Non-metadata status changes can therefore increment generation.

Qualified keys have a required 1..63-character alphanumeric-ended name, with alphanumeric, dash, underscore or dot inside; an optional DNS-subdomain prefix is separated by one slash. Selectors test the labels of their target objects; labels on this parent resource do not replace spec selectors or Pod-template labels. An absent key differs from a present empty value for equality and existence selection.

Full CRD create/replacement bodies decode implicit metadata into ObjectMeta and convert it back to unstructured. ObjectMeta managedFields is omitempty: [] has zero length and is omitted, so it becomes absent before field management; [{}] has one item and survives. Patch transformations require their own path analysis; these complete-body outcomes do not prove every patch format.

Incoming CRD request decoding does not enable malformed-metadata dropping or generation repair. Storage codec decoding enables both for persisted objects. A stored-object repair branch cannot be used to promise acceptance of malformed incoming ObjectMeta.
Argo CD v3.5.2 uses k8s.io/apimachinery v0.36.1; the server operation expectations here are Kubernetes v1.35.0 source, not that client dependency.

The Argo CRD envelopes and opaque metadata inventory remain the pinned chart schema authority. The Kubernetes ObjectMeta reference is a receiving obligation independent of that opacity; it does not add schema properties.

Argo event-label construction uses Application labels first and fills absent keys from its resolved AppProject. A present empty Application label still wins over the project value. Include-key patterns select labels, then exclude-key patterns remove them. Project lookup failure logs a warning and keeps the Application labels. These event labels do not change Kubernetes admission or select application target resources.

AppProject metadata.name is the project identity selected by Application spec.project and Argo RBAC. The project informer is restricted to the control-plane namespace; add/update/delete metadata keys queue project processing and invalidate project cache by name. Direct Kubernetes CRD access does not run Argo server project RBAC.

KubeClaw GitOps bootstrap derives a root name from the first runtime namespace and a separate workload project name. Bootstrap Applications and AppProjects carry kubeclaw.dev/gitops-root. Preflight reads existing objects by name in the selected Argo namespace and rejects a different root label. Its bootstrap-Application exemption also requires matching name, namespace and spec.project. A matching label alone grants neither Kubernetes nor Argo permission. The chart emits kubeclaw.dev/gitops-project on group Applications; spec.project remains the actual Argo project selector.

contract.description:
failurePolicy defines how to handle failures for the admission policy. Failures can occur from CEL expression parse errors, type check errors, runtime errors and invalid or mis-configured policy definitions or bindings.

A policy is invalid if spec.paramKind refers to a non-existent Kind. A binding is invalid if spec.paramRef.name refers to a non-existent resource.

failurePolicy does not define how validations that evaluate to false are handled.

When failurePolicy is set to Fail, ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding validationActions define how failures are enforced.

Allowed values are Ignore or Fail. Defaults to Fail.

cases.condition: the assertion has no individual evaluation error and the overall message filter reports ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget
cases.name: message-filter-preemption
cases.sourceOutcome: Do not use the true or false assertion result. Create an error decision: Ignore gives ActionAdmit; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. A later overall audit-filter error can replace the returned decisions.

cases.condition: the overall audit filter reports an error after assertion decisions were computed
cases.name: audit-filter-replacement
cases.sourceOutcome: Discard those assertion decisions and return one error decision. Ignore gives ActionAdmit even after a false assertion; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. These actions apply to the replacement error, not the discarded assertions.

cases.condition: failurePolicy is Ignore, a validation evaluates false, and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: false-with-ignore
cases.sourceOutcome: The validator returns ActionDeny; the binding maps that decision through Deny, Warn and Audit.

cases.condition: validation CEL evaluation reports an individual error
cases.name: evaluation-error
cases.sourceOutcome: Initially Ignore yields ActionAdmit and Fail yields ActionDeny. A later overall audit-filter error can replace the decisions; only the returned ActionDeny decisions receive binding actions.

cases.condition: a matched policy/binding has a configuration error
cases.name: configuration-error
cases.sourceOutcome: Ignore discards that error. Fail appends a denied decision directly, without consulting validationActions.

cases.condition: an individual audit value result has an error and failurePolicy is Fail
cases.name: audit-expression-error
cases.sourceOutcome: The dispatcher adds a direct denied decision; Audit-only or Warn-only actions do not prevent this denial.

It creates no workload rollout and does not repair earlier stored resources. contract.description:
MatchConditions is a list of conditions that must be met for a request to be validated. Match conditions filter requests that have already been matched by the rules, namespaceSelector, and objectSelector. An empty list of matchConditions matches all requests. There are a maximum of 64 match conditions allowed.

If a parameter object is provided, it can be accessed via the `params` handle in the same manner as validation expressions.

The exact matching logic is (in order):
  1. If ANY matchCondition evaluates to FALSE, the policy is skipped.
  2. If ALL matchConditions evaluate to TRUE, the policy is evaluated.
  3. If any matchCondition evaluates to an error (but none are FALSE):
     - If failurePolicy=Fail, reject the request
     - If failurePolicy=Ignore, the policy is skipped

contract.description:
Resources is a list of resources this rule applies to.

For example: 'pods' means pods. 'pods/log' means the log subresource of pods. '*' means all resources, but not subresources. 'pods/*' means all subresources of pods. '*/scale' means all scale subresources. '*/*' means all resources and their subresources.

If wildcard is present, the validation rule will ensure resources do not overlap with each other.

Depending on the enclosing object, subresources might not be allowed. Required.

cases.condition: apiGroups contains an empty string
cases.name: core-group
cases.sourceOutcome: Accept the core API group; do not treat it as missing.

cases.condition: operations contains * with another item
cases.name: wildcard-operation
cases.sourceOutcome: Reject the rule.

cases.condition: resources is ["pods", "*"]
cases.name: plain-wildcard-order
cases.sourceOutcome: The final * resets the implementation flag, so the plain-resource conflict check does not reject this order. ["*", "pods"] is rejected. Preserve the stricter declared contract.

cases.condition: resources contains pods/status before pods/*
cases.name: wildcard-resource-order
cases.sourceOutcome: The validator does not reject this pair through the earlier-wildcard check. Reversing these items produces an error; */* conflicts are checked across the whole list.

cases.condition: resourceNames is omitted or []
cases.name: no-resource-name
cases.sourceOutcome: A matched rule does not restrict request names.

cases.condition: this is an exclusion and the request matches it
cases.name: exclusion-match
cases.sourceOutcome: Skip the policy or binding before checking inclusion rules.

contract.description: Validations contain CEL expressions which is used to apply the validation. Validations and AuditAnnotations may not both be empty; a minimum of one Validations or AuditAnnotations is required.

cases.condition: the assertion has no individual evaluation error and the overall message filter reports ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget
cases.name: message-filter-preemption
cases.sourceOutcome: Do not use the true or false assertion result. Create an error decision: Ignore gives ActionAdmit; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. A later overall audit-filter error can replace the returned decisions.

cases.condition: the overall audit filter reports an error after assertion decisions were computed
cases.name: audit-filter-replacement
cases.sourceOutcome: Discard those assertion decisions and return one error decision. Ignore gives ActionAdmit even after a false assertion; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. These actions apply to the replacement error, not the discarded assertions.

cases.condition: the expression evaluates true and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: true
cases.sourceOutcome: Return ActionAdmit for this assertion. Other assertion decisions, individual audit errors and admission components can still affect the request.

cases.condition: the expression evaluates false and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: false
cases.sourceOutcome: Apply binding validationActions even if failurePolicy is Ignore.

cases.condition: expression contains a line break, message is absent and the expression otherwise compiles
cases.name: multiline-without-message
cases.sourceOutcome: The validator tests trimmed message for line breaks in both branches; it does not test expression here. Therefore no required-message error is produced by this branch.

cases.condition: a false assertion reaches message selection without a superseding overall message/audit-filter error, and its individual message result is null, has an ordinary evaluation error, or is blank, over 5120 bytes or contains LF after TrimSpace
cases.name: dynamic-message-fallback
cases.sourceOutcome: Use trimmed static message if present; otherwise emit failed expression: followed by the trimmed expression.

cases.condition: a false assertion reaches message selection, the successful individual message result is "\nhello\n", and no overall message/audit-filter error supersedes it
cases.name: dynamic-edge-LF
cases.sourceOutcome: TrimSpace produces hello before LF and size checks. Use hello as the dynamic failure message.

cases.condition: a false assertion reaches message selection, its successfully evaluated dynamic string exceeds 5120 bytes only because of surrounding whitespace, its trimmed content is nonempty and at most 5120 bytes with no LF, and no overall message/audit-filter error supersedes it
cases.name: dynamic-raw-long-trimmed-short
cases.sourceOutcome: The size check uses the trimmed content, so this string is usable as the dynamic failure message.

cases.condition: a static message has CR or LF only at its edges, and its trimmed content is nonempty with no internal line break
cases.name: static-edge-linebreak
cases.sourceOutcome: The validator checks the trimmed message and accepts this branch. If the static message is selected for a false assertion and no overall message/audit-filter error supersedes that result, runtime emits the trimmed static message.

cases.condition: a dynamic message contains an internal CR but no LF and otherwise passes the size/nonblank checks
cases.name: dynamic-internal-CR
cases.sourceOutcome: The runtime message check tests LF only; it does not reject this CR through that branch, unlike the static-message validator.

cases.condition: the assertion has no individual evaluation error and the overall message filter reports ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget
cases.name: dynamic-message-budget
cases.sourceOutcome: Preempt assertion truth with an error decision: Ignore gives ActionAdmit; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. This is separate from an individual message error that falls back.

cases.condition: reason is Unauthorized
cases.name: reason-Unauthorized
cases.sourceOutcome: Reject the policy, despite the v1 type comment listing this reason.

receiverContract.changeImpact: A valid spec change increments generation and updates later policy matching/evaluation after informer refresh. Changing this field can widen, narrow or alter admission decisions; inspect every matching binding and parameter before the change. Recovery uses an authorized, version-checked change to the owning policy/binding; confirm the observed spec and effective requests before treating the recovery as complete.
crossFieldConditions: CEL means Common Expression Language. Validation expressions use object, oldObject, request, namespaceObject and authorizer; params is declared only with paramKind. CREATE has null oldObject; DELETE has null object. namespaceObject is null for cluster-scoped requests. Composition exposes earlier variables as variables.<name>. Guard null and absent properties before access. Each policy/binding/parameter validation evaluation starts with 10000000 CEL cost units; message expressions use its remaining budget. Audit expressions receive a separate 10000000-unit budget. Match conditions receive 2500000 units. These are work budgets, not response-time guarantees.

Create checks use the NewExpressions environment. Update reuses the StoredExpressions environment for unchanged expression strings found in the old policy. Runtime compiles persisted expressions in StoredExpressions. This compatibility rule does not bypass checks on changed expressions.

An overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget is handled before assertion truth when that assertion has no individual evaluation error. An overall audit-filter error replaces all computed assertion decisions with one error decision. Ignore maps these errors to ActionAdmit, even after a false assertion; Fail maps them to ActionDeny for binding action enforcement. Other policy/parameter evaluations and admission components remain separate.

The admission compiler uses dynamic object types. Separate controller type checking reports warnings for selected resource schemas and does not change enforcement; its warnings are not proof that every wildcard or alternative was checked.
Validation and message expressions share composed variables. Message expressions have no authorizer; do not expose information through the response message without an appropriate policy.

cases.condition: the assertion has no individual evaluation error and the overall message filter reports ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget
cases.name: message-filter-preemption
cases.sourceOutcome: Do not use the true or false assertion result. Create an error decision: Ignore gives ActionAdmit; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. A later overall audit-filter error can replace the returned decisions.

cases.condition: the overall audit filter reports an error after assertion decisions were computed
cases.name: audit-filter-replacement
cases.sourceOutcome: Discard those assertion decisions and return one error decision. Ignore gives ActionAdmit even after a false assertion; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. These actions apply to the replacement error, not the discarded assertions.

cases.condition: the expression evaluates true and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: true
cases.sourceOutcome: Return ActionAdmit for this assertion. Other assertion decisions, individual audit errors and admission components can still affect the request.

cases.condition: the expression evaluates false and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: false
cases.sourceOutcome: Apply binding validationActions even if failurePolicy is Ignore.

cases.condition: expression contains a line break, message is absent and the expression otherwise compiles
cases.name: multiline-without-message
cases.sourceOutcome: The validator tests trimmed message for line breaks in both branches; it does not test expression here. Therefore no required-message error is produced by this branch.

cases.condition: a false assertion reaches message selection without a superseding overall message/audit-filter error, and its individual message result is null, has an ordinary evaluation error, or is blank, over 5120 bytes or contains LF after TrimSpace
cases.name: dynamic-message-fallback
cases.sourceOutcome: Use trimmed static message if present; otherwise emit failed expression: followed by the trimmed expression.

cases.condition: a false assertion reaches message selection, the successful individual message result is "\nhello\n", and no overall message/audit-filter error supersedes it
cases.name: dynamic-edge-LF
cases.sourceOutcome: TrimSpace produces hello before LF and size checks. Use hello as the dynamic failure message.

cases.condition: a false assertion reaches message selection, its successfully evaluated dynamic string exceeds 5120 bytes only because of surrounding whitespace, its trimmed content is nonempty and at most 5120 bytes with no LF, and no overall message/audit-filter error supersedes it
cases.name: dynamic-raw-long-trimmed-short
cases.sourceOutcome: The size check uses the trimmed content, so this string is usable as the dynamic failure message.

cases.condition: a static message has CR or LF only at its edges, and its trimmed content is nonempty with no internal line break
cases.name: static-edge-linebreak
cases.sourceOutcome: The validator checks the trimmed message and accepts this branch. If the static message is selected for a false assertion and no overall message/audit-filter error supersedes that result, runtime emits the trimmed static message.

cases.condition: a dynamic message contains an internal CR but no LF and otherwise passes the size/nonblank checks
cases.name: dynamic-internal-CR
cases.sourceOutcome: The runtime message check tests LF only; it does not reject this CR through that branch, unlike the static-message validator.

cases.condition: the assertion has no individual evaluation error and the overall message filter reports ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget
cases.name: dynamic-message-budget
cases.sourceOutcome: Preempt assertion truth with an error decision: Ignore gives ActionAdmit; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. This is separate from an individual message error that falls back.

cases.condition: reason is Unauthorized
cases.name: reason-Unauthorized
cases.sourceOutcome: Reject the policy, despite the v1 type comment listing this reason.

receiverContract.changeImpact: A valid spec change increments generation and updates later policy matching/evaluation after informer refresh. Changing this field can widen, narrow or alter admission decisions; inspect every matching binding and parameter before the change. It creates no workload rollout and does not repair earlier stored resources. Recovery uses an authorized, version-checked change to the owning policy/binding; confirm the observed spec and effective requests before treating the recovery as complete.
crossFieldConditions: CEL means Common Expression Language. Validation expressions use object, oldObject, request, namespaceObject and authorizer; params is declared only with paramKind. CREATE has null oldObject; DELETE has null object. namespaceObject is null for cluster-scoped requests. Composition exposes earlier variables as variables.<name>. Guard null and absent properties before access. Each policy/binding/parameter validation evaluation starts with 10000000 CEL cost units; message expressions use its remaining budget. Audit expressions receive a separate 10000000-unit budget. Match conditions receive 2500000 units. These are work budgets, not response-time guarantees.

Create checks use the NewExpressions environment. Update reuses the StoredExpressions environment for unchanged expression strings found in the old policy. Runtime compiles persisted expressions in StoredExpressions. This compatibility rule does not bypass checks on changed expressions.

An overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget is handled before assertion truth when that assertion has no individual evaluation error. An overall audit-filter error replaces all computed assertion decisions with one error decision. Ignore maps these errors to ActionAdmit, even after a false assertion; Fail maps them to ActionDeny for binding action enforcement. Other policy/parameter evaluations and admission components remain separate.

The admission compiler uses dynamic object types. Separate controller type checking reports warnings for selected resource schemas and does not change enforcement; its warnings are not proof that every wildcard or alternative was checked.
Validation and message expressions share composed variables. Message expressions have no authorizer; do not expose information through the response message without an appropriate policy.

contract.description:
Expression represents the expression which will be evaluated by CEL. ref: https://github.com/google/cel-spec CEL expressions have access to the contents of the API request/response, organized into CEL variables as well as some other useful variables:

- 'object' - The object from the incoming request. The value is null for DELETE requests. - 'oldObject' - The existing object. The value is null for CREATE requests. - 'request' - Attributes of the API request([ref](/pkg/apis/admission/types.go#AdmissionRequest)). - 'params' - Parameter resource referred to by the policy binding being evaluated. Only populated if the policy has a ParamKind. - 'namespaceObject' - The namespace object that the incoming object belongs to. The value is null for cluster-scoped resources. - 'variables' - Map of composited variables, from its name to its lazily evaluated value.
  For example, a variable named 'foo' can be accessed as 'variables.foo'.
- 'authorizer' - A CEL Authorizer. May be used to perform authorization checks for the principal (user or service account) of the request.
  See https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/library#Authz
- 'authorizer.requestResource' - A CEL ResourceCheck constructed from the 'authorizer' and configured with the
  request resource.

The `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.name` and `metadata.generateName` are always accessible from the root of the object. No other metadata properties are accessible.

Only property names of the form `[a-zA-Z_.-/][a-zA-Z0-9_.-/]*` are accessible. Accessible property names are escaped according to the following rules when accessed in the expression: - '__' escapes to '__underscores__' - '.' escapes to '__dot__' - '-' escapes to '__dash__' - '/' escapes to '__slash__' - Property names that exactly match a CEL RESERVED keyword escape to '__{keyword}__'. The keywords are:
	  "true", "false", "null", "in", "as", "break", "const", "continue", "else", "for", "function", "if",
	  "import", "let", "loop", "package", "namespace", "return".
Examples:
  - Expression accessing a property named "namespace": {"Expression": "object.__namespace__ > 0"}
  - Expression accessing a property named "x-prop": {"Expression": "object.x__dash__prop > 0"}
  - Expression accessing a property named "redact__d": {"Expression": "object.redact__underscores__d > 0"}

Equality on arrays with list type of 'set' or 'map' ignores element order, i.e. [1, 2] == [2, 1]. Concatenation on arrays with x-kubernetes-list-type use the semantics of the list type:
  - 'set': `X + Y` performs a union where the array positions of all elements in `X` are preserved and
    non-intersecting elements in `Y` are appended, retaining their partial order.
  - 'map': `X + Y` performs a merge where the array positions of all keys in `X` are preserved but the values
    are overwritten by values in `Y` when the key sets of `X` and `Y` intersect. Elements in `Y` with
    non-intersecting keys are appended, retaining their partial order.
Required.

contract.description:
Variables contain definitions of variables that can be used in composition of other expressions. Each variable is defined as a named CEL expression. The variables defined here will be available under `variables` in other expressions of the policy except MatchConditions because MatchConditions are evaluated before the rest of the policy.

The expression of a variable can refer to other variables defined earlier in the list but not those after. Thus, Variables must be sorted by the order of first appearance and acyclic.

cases.condition: a variable expression references an earlier valid variable
cases.name: earlier-reference
cases.sourceOutcome: Its declaration is available during compilation.

cases.condition: a variable references a field only declared later
cases.name: later-reference
cases.sourceOutcome: Compilation cannot resolve that field at this point and rejects the expression.

cases.condition: two independently compilable variables have the same valid name
cases.name: duplicate-name
cases.sourceOutcome: validateVariable does not reject duplication. CompileAndStoreVariable overwrites that name in CompiledVariables; this conflicts with the v1 unique-name contract.

cases.condition: no expression accesses the variable
cases.name: unused-value
cases.sourceOutcome: The lazy runtime value is not evaluated, although its definition is compiled.

cases.condition: a new matchCondition refers to variables
cases.name: match-condition-variable
cases.sourceOutcome: Stateless create validation does not declare variables. Runtime compilation of a persisted policy uses composition; this is an implementation discrepancy, not a supported create bypass.

receiverContract.changeImpact: A valid spec change increments generation and updates later policy matching/evaluation after informer refresh. Changing this field can widen, narrow or alter admission decisions; inspect every matching binding and parameter before the change. It creates no workload rollout and does not repair earlier stored resources. Recovery uses an authorized, version-checked change to the owning policy/binding; confirm the observed spec and effective requests before treating the recovery as complete.
crossFieldConditions: CEL means Common Expression Language. Validation expressions use object, oldObject, request, namespaceObject and authorizer; params is declared only with paramKind. CREATE has null oldObject; DELETE has null object. namespaceObject is null for cluster-scoped requests. Composition exposes earlier variables as variables.<name>. Guard null and absent properties before access. Each policy/binding/parameter validation evaluation starts with 10000000 CEL cost units; message expressions use its remaining budget. Audit expressions receive a separate 10000000-unit budget. Match conditions receive 2500000 units. These are work budgets, not response-time guarantees.

Variable create checks use NewExpressions. On update, a variable expression uses StoredExpressions only if its exact string equals an old validation expression; old variable expressions are not collected by findValidatingPolicyPreexistingExpressions. Runtime compiles persisted variables in StoredExpressions.

Variable compilation occurs in list order; earlier declarations are available to later ones. Values are evaluated lazily. The runtime compiler stores compiled variables by name; a later duplicate overwrites the earlier entry.

The v1 contract excludes variables from matchConditions. Create validation uses a stateless compiler for those conditions. Runtime compilePolicy instead gives matchConditions the composition compiler; do not rely on this runtime discrepancy to author a policy that create validation rejects.

contract.description:
ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding binds the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with paramerized resources. ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding and parameter CRDs together define how cluster administrators configure policies for clusters.

For a given admission request, each binding will cause its policy to be evaluated N times, where N is 1 for policies/bindings that don't use params, otherwise N is the number of parameters selected by the binding.

The CEL expressions of a policy must have a computed CEL cost below the maximum CEL budget. Each evaluation of the policy is given an independent CEL cost budget. Adding/removing policies, bindings, or params can not affect whether a given (policy, binding, param) combination is within its own CEL budget.

contract.description:
validationActions declares how Validations of the referenced ValidatingAdmissionPolicy are enforced. If a validation evaluates to false it is always enforced according to these actions.

Failures defined by the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy's FailurePolicy are enforced according to these actions only if the FailurePolicy is set to Fail, otherwise the failures are ignored. This includes compilation errors, runtime errors and misconfigurations of the policy.

validationActions is declared as a set of action values. Order does not matter. validationActions may not contain duplicates of the same action.

The supported actions values are:

"Deny" specifies that a validation failure results in a denied request.

"Warn" specifies that a validation failure is reported to the request client in HTTP Warning headers, with a warning code of 299. Warnings can be sent both for allowed or denied admission responses.

"Audit" specifies that a validation failure is included in the published audit event for the request. The audit event will contain a `validation.policy.admission.k8s.io/validation_failure` audit annotation with a value containing the details of the validation failures, formatted as a JSON list of objects, each with the following fields: - message: The validation failure message string - policy: The resource name of the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy - binding: The resource name of the ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding - expressionIndex: The index of the failed validations in the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy - validationActions: The enforcement actions enacted for the validation failure Example audit annotation: `"validation.policy.admission.k8s.io/validation_failure": "[{\"message\": \"Invalid value\", {\"policy\": \"policy.example.com\", {\"binding\": \"policybinding.example.com\", {\"expressionIndex\": \"1\", {\"validationActions\": [\"Audit\"]}]"`

Clients should expect to handle additional values by ignoring any values not recognized.

"Deny" and "Warn" may not be used together since this combination needlessly duplicates the validation failure both in the API response body and the HTTP warning headers.

Required.

cases.condition: the assertion has no individual evaluation error and the overall message filter reports ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget
cases.name: message-filter-preemption
cases.sourceOutcome: Do not use the true or false assertion result. Create an error decision: Ignore gives ActionAdmit; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. A later overall audit-filter error can replace the returned decisions.

cases.condition: the overall audit filter reports an error after assertion decisions were computed
cases.name: audit-filter-replacement
cases.sourceOutcome: Discard those assertion decisions and return one error decision. Ignore gives ActionAdmit even after a false assertion; Fail gives ActionDeny for binding actions. These actions apply to the replacement error, not the discarded assertions.

cases.condition: a validation is false, actions includes Deny, and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: Deny
cases.sourceOutcome: Append a denied decision and reject the request.

cases.condition: a validation is false, actions includes Warn, and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: Warn
cases.sourceOutcome: Add an HTTP warning through the server warning mechanism; this action alone does not deny.

cases.condition: a validation is false, actions includes Audit, and the assertion has no individual evaluation error, no overall message-filter ErrInternal or ErrOutOfBudget preempts its result, and no overall audit-filter error replaces the decisions
cases.name: Audit
cases.sourceOutcome: Publish a validation.policy.admission.k8s.io/validation_failure annotation with message, policy, binding, expressionIndex and validationActions.

cases.condition: a returned ActionDeny decision exists and the configured action set is either [Deny, Audit] or [Warn, Audit]
cases.name: combined-actions
cases.sourceOutcome: Perform both configured actions.

cases.condition: actions contains both Deny and Warn
cases.name: invalid-combination
cases.sourceOutcome: Reject the binding.

cases.sourceOutcome: The normal Deployment strategy clears status at create or preserves stored status on update, drops fields only under their actual disabled-gate/old-use predicates, and validates selector, rollout settings and the whole Pod template. Failed child/default/OS/cross-field checks reject the parent; optional omitted parents are not materialized merely to run a child case. Accepted template changes are copied into a hashed ReplicaSet, whose create validator has no old template; new Pod create validation likewise has no old spec. A Deployment update compatibility option does not transfer to those child creates, and ReplicaSet rejection stops the route before Pod creation. Accepted child templates then reach new Pods; replica-only/pause/controller-setting updates instead use their selected scaling/rollout routes. Pod creation applies its distinct defaults and configured admission (ServiceAccount/token, Priority, RuntimeClass and selectors), then placement uses the chosen scheduler profile, gates, taints, affinity and resource/DRA accounting. On the chosen node, DNS/hostname/hosts and namespaces are assembled, image policy/user/security are resolved, claims/volumes/mounts/devices and projected identities are prepared, then ordered init actions precede regular-container start and lifecycle/probe state governs readiness, restart and grace. A failure at any selected API/admission/scheduler/node boundary prevents the corresponding later success; controller observation counts and conditions report their own asynchronous state. Recovery belongs to the owner of that failed boundary and must verify its next observation; template updates do not rewrite existing Pods/claims. Conditional legacy storage product limits, including selected vSphere inline storagePolicyName nil dereference, remain explicit static limits rather than executed panics or general migration claims. Full Deployment completeness also requires every routed metadata/envelope receiver and each original context; this spec-provider parent sequence neither supplies nor waives that separate authority. Integration must join all 1389 paths, including the 104 metadata/envelope paths, before full receiver acceptance. Source contracts distinguish available implementation from target API/gate/image/driver/issuer/node inputs; Unit export checks and Live acceptance are separate.

validateCommonFields runs both create-style common metadata validation and metadata update validation.
BeforeUpdate enforces request namespace, restores generation, prepares the resource, fills an absent UID, preserves existing creation/deletion timestamps and absent deletion grace, then validates.
Create-handler wiping clears system lifecycle metadata; store initialization sets current creation time and a new UUID.
Scope matching fills an absent namespace, clears namespace for a cluster request, and rejects unequal nonempty namespace values.
Store create initializes system metadata and generates a name before BeforeCreate and admission validation.

cases.name: rollout-scaling-and-fenceposts
cases.sourceOutcome: RollingUpdate scales the new ReplicaSet up only within desired replicas + rounded-up surge, and not beyond the desired new replica count. maxUnavailable percentages round down; if both resolved fenceposts are zero, the helper makes unavailable=1. Old-scale reduction subtracts minimum availability and unavailable new replicas; unhealthy old replicas are considered first. Recreate first scales old ReplicaSets to zero and waits for old running Pods before creating/scaling the new ReplicaSet. Paused Deployments still use the scaling sync path, while template rollout is deferred. ReplicaSet update/API errors return to reconciliation; desired count is not proof that Pods ran.

cases.condition: The controller reconciles zero or MaxInt32 revisionHistoryLimit, an elapsed progress deadline, or pause/resume.
cases.name: history-and-progress-sentinels
cases.sourceOutcome: revisionHistoryLimit=2147483647 disables finite-history cleanup. Zero permits cleanup of all eligible old ReplicaSets, but only nondeleting sets with zero desired/actual replicas and observed generation caught up can be deleted; oldest revisions are considered first and a non-NotFound delete error stops cleanup. progressDeadlineSeconds=2147483647 disables progress-deadline reporting. Otherwise missing Progressing cannot establish a timeout, a completed NewReplicaSetAvailable reason suppresses timeout, and existing ProgressDeadlineExceeded remains timed out. New updates/readiness/availability or fewer old replicas count as progress; absent progress beyond LastUpdateTime+deadline sets Progressing=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded. This publisher does not perform automatic rollback. Pause writes Progressing=Unknown/DeploymentPaused and resume writes Unknown/DeploymentResumed to restart progress accounting, except an existing timed-out reason is preserved. Operators must inspect the condition and failing ReplicaSet/Pod, fix the dependency or choose an explicit rollout change; elapsed time alone does not restore availability.

cases.condition: Current counts show progress, completion or lack of progress; ReplicaSet reconciliation may fail and a Deployment may pause/resume.
cases.name: status-progress-condition-publishers
cases.sourceOutcome: Available becomes True/MinimumReplicasAvailable when available replicas meet desired-MaxUnavailable, otherwise False/MinimumReplicasUnavailable. New/found ReplicaSets publish True/NewReplicaSetCreated or True/FoundNewReplicaSet; API creation failures publish False/ReplicaSetCreateError when progress deadlines are tracked. Rollout completion publishes True/NewReplicaSetAvailable; increasing updated/ready/available or reducing old replicas publishes True/ReplicaSetUpdated. For this progress case, the publisher removes the old condition before setting the new one, so LastUpdateTime changes even when status and reason remain the same; an existing True status preserves LastTransitionTime. The generic SetDeploymentCondition helper otherwise skips unchanged status/reason and preserves transition time for unchanged status. A tracked elapsed deadline publishes False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded; disabled/no deadline removes Progressing. Pause/resume publish Unknown/DeploymentPaused or Unknown/DeploymentResumed except an existing timeout is not overwritten. ReplicaFailure copies the new ReplicaSet failure in preference to old sets; none removes the Deployment failure condition. Status update errors return to reconciliation, while unchanged stuck status schedules a later requeue. Timeout reporting does not implement automatic rollback. Controller timestamps/reasons diagnose a specific publisher, not a freshness guarantee for all workloads.

contract.description: Variable references $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the previously defined environment variables in the container and any service environment variables. If a variable cannot be resolved, the reference in the input string will be unchanged. Restart eligibility uses the container policy when ContainerRestartRules is enabled, otherwise Pod policy; exit-code rules are not evaluated for this still-running probe failure. The workload owner must distinguish request construction, network/TLS/redirect and status failures before changing thresholds; a probe success does not prove a complete business operation.

contract.description:
Quantity is a fixed-point representation of a number. It provides convenient marshaling/unmarshaling in JSON and YAML, in addition to String() and AsInt64() accessors.

The serialization format is:

``` <quantity>        ::= <signedNumber><suffix>

	(Note that <suffix> may be empty, from the "" case in <decimalSI>.)

<digit>           ::= 0 | 1 | ... | 9 <digits>          ::= <digit> | <digit><digits> <number>          ::= <digits> | <digits>.<digits> | <digits>. | .<digits> <sign>            ::= "+" | "-" <signedNumber>    ::= <number> | <sign><number> <suffix>          ::= <binarySI> | <decimalExponent> | <decimalSI> <binarySI>        ::= Ki | Mi | Gi | Ti | Pi | Ei

	(International System of units; See: http://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Units/binary.html)

<decimalSI>       ::= m | "" | k | M | G | T | P | E

	(Note that 1024 = 1Ki but 1000 = 1k; I didn't choose the capitalization.)

<decimalExponent> ::= "e" <signedNumber> | "E" <signedNumber> ```

No matter which of the three exponent forms is used, no quantity may represent a number greater than 2^63-1 in magnitude, nor may it have more than 3 decimal places. Numbers larger or more precise will be capped or rounded up. (E.g.: 0.1m will rounded up to 1m.) This may be extended in the future if we require larger or smaller quantities.

When a Quantity is parsed from a string, it will remember the type of suffix it had, and will use the same type again when it is serialized.

Before serializing, Quantity will be put in "canonical form". This means that Exponent/suffix will be adjusted up or down (with a corresponding increase or decrease in Mantissa) such that:

- No precision is lost - No fractional digits will be emitted - The exponent (or suffix) is as large as possible.

The sign will be omitted unless the number is negative.

Examples:

- 1.5 will be serialized as "1500m" - 1.5Gi will be serialized as "1536Mi"

Note that the quantity will NEVER be internally represented by a floating point number. That is the whole point of this exercise.

Non-canonical values will still parse as long as they are well formed, but will be re-emitted in their canonical form. (So always use canonical form, or don't diff.)

This format is intended to make it difficult to use these numbers without writing some sort of special handling code in the hopes that that will cause implementors to also use a fixed point implementation.

contract.description:
Quantity is a fixed-point representation of a number. It provides convenient marshaling/unmarshaling in JSON and YAML, in addition to String() and AsInt64() accessors.

The serialization format is:

``` <quantity>        ::= <signedNumber><suffix>

	(Note that <suffix> may be empty, from the "" case in <decimalSI>.)

<digit>           ::= 0 | 1 | ... | 9 <digits>          ::= <digit> | <digit><digits> <number>          ::= <digits> | <digits>.<digits> | <digits>. | .<digits> <sign>            ::= "+" | "-" <signedNumber>    ::= <number> | <sign><number> <suffix>          ::= <binarySI> | <decimalExponent> | <decimalSI> <binarySI>        ::= Ki | Mi | Gi | Ti | Pi | Ei

	(International System of units; See: http://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Units/binary.html)

<decimalSI>       ::= m | "" | k | M | G | T | P | E

	(Note that 1024 = 1Ki but 1000 = 1k; I didn't choose the capitalization.)

<decimalExponent> ::= "e" <signedNumber> | "E" <signedNumber> ```

No matter which of the three exponent forms is used, no quantity may represent a number greater than 2^63-1 in magnitude, nor may it have more than 3 decimal places. Numbers larger or more precise will be capped or rounded up. (E.g.: 0.1m will rounded up to 1m.) This may be extended in the future if we require larger or smaller quantities.

When a Quantity is parsed from a string, it will remember the type of suffix it had, and will use the same type again when it is serialized.

Before serializing, Quantity will be put in "canonical form". This means that Exponent/suffix will be adjusted up or down (with a corresponding increase or decrease in Mantissa) such that:

- No precision is lost - No fractional digits will be emitted - The exponent (or suffix) is as large as possible.

The sign will be omitted unless the number is negative.

Examples:

- 1.5 will be serialized as "1500m" - 1.5Gi will be serialized as "1536Mi"

Note that the quantity will NEVER be internally represented by a floating point number. That is the whole point of this exercise.

Non-canonical values will still parse as long as they are well formed, but will be re-emitted in their canonical form. (So always use canonical form, or don't diff.)

This format is intended to make it difficult to use these numbers without writing some sort of special handling code in the hopes that that will cause implementors to also use a fixed point implementation.

contract.description: StartupProbe indicates that the Pod has successfully initialized. If specified, no other probes are executed until this completes successfully. If this probe fails, the Pod will be restarted, just as if the livenessProbe failed. This can be used to provide different probe parameters at the beginning of a Pod's lifecycle, when it might take a long time to load data or warm a cache, than during steady-state operation. This cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-probes

contract.description: Optional duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully. May be decreased in delete request. Value must be non-negative integer.
