receiverContract.changeImpact: An accepted change alters stored metadata or its later consumer input. Read the response and observe the relevant controller; schema or metadata acceptance alone does not prove reconciliation.
crossFieldConditions: These JSON cases decode a fresh ObjectMeta with its immediate parent present. Missing ancestors prevent child decoding. They do not define JSON merge-patch null deletion or apply omission; those operations merge before validation and ownership processing.

REST create decodes and defaults, wipes client system metadata, runs ownership/admission and enters the store. The store sets UID/creation time and generated name, then BeforeCreate enforces scope and strategy/common validation before storage. A validation failure establishes no stored object.

Replacement update uses the current storage object, checks resourceVersion, restores generation before strategy preparation, fills an omitted UID and preserves lifecycle values before common/resource validation. A stale nonempty version returns Conflict; fetch again and recompute the intended change.

Labels and annotations are ordinary readable resource metadata, not Secret storage. Do not place bearer tokens, passwords or private keys here; use the authorized Secret reference appropriate to the consumer and redact metadata when collecting diagnostics.

Authentication, authorization, admission mutation, storage failures and actual controller configuration remain independent boundaries. On an uncertain create response, read by returned/intended identity before retry; generateName retry can create another object if the first call committed.

The CRD strategy sets generation 1 on create. On update it preserves configured status first and increments generation if content other than metadata changes. Metadata-only label/annotation/finalizer changes do not increment it.

The pinned Argo CRDs do not declare a status subresource. Status remains ordinary schema data, written with whole-resource patches; the CRD status reset route described separately is not an installed Argo status endpoint. Non-metadata status changes can therefore increment generation.

Full CRD create/replacement bodies decode implicit metadata into ObjectMeta and convert it back to unstructured. ObjectMeta managedFields is omitempty: [] has zero length and is omitted, so it becomes absent before field management; [{}] has one item and survives. Patch transformations require their own path analysis; these complete-body outcomes do not prove every patch format.

Incoming CRD request decoding does not enable malformed-metadata dropping or generation repair. Storage codec decoding enables both for persisted objects. A stored-object repair branch cannot be used to promise acceptance of malformed incoming ObjectMeta.
Argo CD v3.5.2 uses k8s.io/apimachinery v0.36.1; the server operation expectations here are Kubernetes v1.35.0 source, not that client dependency.

The Argo CRD envelopes and opaque metadata inventory remain the pinned chart schema authority. The Kubernetes ObjectMeta reference is a receiving obligation independent of that opacity; it does not add schema properties.

Argo event-label construction uses Application labels first and fills absent keys from its resolved AppProject. A present empty Application label still wins over the project value. Include-key patterns select labels, then exclude-key patterns remove them. Project lookup failure logs a warning and keeps the Application labels. These event labels do not change Kubernetes admission or select application target resources.

Application name/namespace forms QualifiedName for queues, InstanceName for resource/cache identity and RBACName together with its selected project. AppProject access and allowed Application namespaces remain separate from Kubernetes resource authorization.

The Application informer queues namespace/name keys for add, update and delete events after canProcessApp permits the object. Updates request refresh by QualifiedName; an equal resourceVersion can add configured jitter. Queueing and cache identity do not establish a successful reconciliation. Kubernetes client operations and Argo namespace/project authorization must still permit the selected object.

For an Application generated by ApplicationSet, its controller reads the current object and prepares the desired metadata. Configured preserved label and annotation keys keep their existing values, including empty strings; the callback then replaces the label and annotation maps with the prepared maps. IgnoreApplicationDifferences can remove changes from the patch. Equal results skip a write; read, preparation and patch errors do not establish persistence.

The ApplicationSet child-event comparison checks spec, labels, annotations and finalizers, treating nil and empty maps/lists as equal. Resource-version or generation changes alone do not trigger this comparison. Progressive-sync mode separately checks selected health, sync and operation-state observations. This event filter is distinct from admission and successful reconciliation.

ApplicationSet preserves existing pre-delete and post-delete finalizer prefixes, including staged suffixes, when preparing an Application. This preservation does not apply to every token. For an obsolete Application with an invalid destination, its deletion helper removes only the exact foreground resources finalizer before DELETE; background and other tokens are retained. A removed token does not establish target cleanup.

ApplicationSet indexes an Application by the name of a controller reference with its expected group/version and kind, then lists that name within the ApplicationSet namespace. The named index/query does not compare owner UID. When the ApplicationSet is deleting and its effective policy disallows deletion, the selected helper clears the entire ownerReferences list on each returned Application and updates it; a list or update error stops that helper. Inspect the actual owner UID and returned objects before relying on preservation or repeating an interrupted change.

ApplicationSet RollingSync uses generated Application labels to select rollout steps. A missing key with operator In excludes the Application from that step. One Application can match more than one step; this code warns about repeated selection. This consumer is separate from Kubernetes Pod selectors and requires the ApplicationSet strategy and controller.

The Argo Application updateApp helper merges new labels/annotations into the stored maps when its merge argument is true; otherwise it replaces those maps with the new maps. This server operation is distinct from a direct Kubernetes full replacement or patch. Inspect the chosen server request before assuming that an omitted key is retained.

The hydrate annotation requests hydration for any present value, with exact hard selecting hard hydration. Hydration status persistence consumes the annotation. Application summary includes link-prefix annotation values as external links; that collection code does not validate the values as URLs. The separate managed-by-url validator skips missing/empty values and reports InvalidSpecError for an invalid external URL. These consumer rules do not replace general annotation syntax or byte limits.

Application manifest-generate-paths is forwarded to manifest generation. With a prior synced revision, repository depth zero and a nonempty annotation, this controller requests path-specific revision updating. An empty value does not select that optimization; repository failures still return errors.

The manifest-generate-paths consumer splits a nonempty annotation on semicolons, trims whitespace and skips empty entries. On the Linux repository server, a leading slash selects a repository-root path; a relative entry is joined to the source path and cleaned. A configured hydration sync source instead selects its own source path and ignores this annotation. These paths select refresh work, not access authorization.

Webhook refresh also requires a matching repository URL and changed source revision. When either the changed-file list or selected path list is empty, the path matcher requires refresh. Otherwise it tests exact paths, descendants and filepath patterns. A match queues refresh, with optional jitter; it does not prove completed generation, synchronization or hydration. An unmatched change can still update manifest-cache revision keys when cache warming is enabled.

argocd.argoproj.io/refresh requests normal refresh for any present value except exact hard, which selects hard refresh. Absence does not request refresh; empty/unknown values still request normal refresh. Reconciliation persistence removes this key after the refresh. The skip-reconcile annotation uses ParseBool: true stops processing, false continues and invalid/empty text logs then continues.

Deletion confirmation uses the deletion-approved annotation timestamp: missing, empty or invalid RFC3339 does not approve; a valid timestamp at or after deletion start approves. This does not waive Kubernetes admission or target cleanup.

Application resource finalizers select controller cleanup, separate from the API GC finalizers. The controller rereads the Application, resolves project/target access, runs pre-delete hooks, waits for deletion confirmation/pending live deletion, deletes permitted resources with selected foreground/background policy, rereads remaining resources and only then removes its cascade token. Post-delete hooks retain their own tokens while incomplete.

If destination-cluster lookup fails, this pinned Argo branch removes cascade/pre/post-delete tokens and returns after updating finalizers; it does not prove target resources were cleaned up. Other target access, hook, list or delete errors can retain tokens. Recovery must inspect Application and target state before repeating destructive work.

continuousApplications removes any stale immutable-bundle-path annotation and writes the selected path only for a unique releases/gitops/<bundle>/{buster,nova,prism} directory with resources.yaml. The platform health Lua uses that equality only when a successful applied operation has another revision than the currently compared main revision. Healthy/synced state, successful operation and matching applied repoURL/path/targetRevision/directory include remain required. The marker affects reported health, not synchronization, ownership or content immutability.

KubeClaw GitOps bootstrap derives a root name from the first runtime namespace and a separate workload project name. Bootstrap Applications and AppProjects carry kubeclaw.dev/gitops-root. Preflight reads existing objects by name in the selected Argo namespace and rejects a different root label. Its bootstrap-Application exemption also requires matching name, namespace and spec.project. A matching label alone grants neither Kubernetes nor Argo permission. The chart emits kubeclaw.dev/gitops-project on group Applications; spec.project remains the actual Argo project selector.

KubeClaw authors argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave=-1 on bootstrap AppProjects and the supported GitOps chart copies each group wave to its Application. The parent sync engine parses the annotation with Atoi and orders by phase before wave, then kind and name. Missing or invalid wave text falls back to Helm hook weight, then zero when that weight is absent or invalid. A wave orders the parent resource tasks; it does not directly synchronize the child workload or bypass its project and health checks.

The maintained SPIRE Application selects compare-options=ServerSideDiff=true. Argo splits the annotation on commas, trims entries, ignores empty entries and matches exact options. ServerSideDiff=true enables server-side comparison unless ServerSideDiff=false is also present, which takes precedence. Omission leaves the controller setting in effect. A successful dry-run comparison does not persist the target or establish synchronization.

Platform child Applications carry ignore-healthcheck=true and kubeclaw.io/health-mode=observed. Only the exact string true makes the parent health aggregator skip that live child; this does not stop the child controller or make it healthy. The installed KubeClaw Lua health customization first reports selected comparison/sync errors and failed operations as Degraded. After those checks, exact observed reports stored child health without requiring synchronization to its selected revision. Other values use the strict source/revision/destination/operation checks. The customization must be installed in the actual Argo configuration.

The bootstrap runtime-namespaces annotation is a JSON array of valid GitOps namespace names. claimedNamespaces parses it and combines it with spec.destination.namespace; absent annotation contributes no extra namespace. Invalid JSON or a non-array/invalid name fails the ownership check. Bootstrap preflight requires the stored annotation text to match the newly generated claim and rejects a changed repository or namespace claim. The group chart serializes helm-releases for release context; the prerequisite check reads the bundle group helmReleases rather than trusting that annotation. Neither annotation transfers ownership or removes retained resources.

ApplicationSet combines configured preserved label/annotation keys and copies their existing values into the generated maps.
The ApplicationSet callback assigns prepared annotation, label and finalizer values and sets its controller reference.
CreateOrUpdate reads the Application, handles NotFound through preparation/create, and propagates read or preparation errors.
For an existing Application, CreateOrUpdate normalizes live spec, applies ignored differences, skips equal results and otherwise merge-patches with propagated errors.
ApplicationSet child-event comparison checks spec, labels, annotations and finalizers with empty equivalence; progressive-sync mode additionally checks selected status observations.
Default preserved finalizer prefixes are the pre-delete and post-delete tokens.
ApplicationSet appends existing matching finalizer prefixes to the generated finalizers before assigning the prepared metadata.
Deletion of an obsolete generated Application first calls the invalid-destination finalizer helper; a helper error stops that Application DELETE.
The finalizer helper checks whether the destination resolves and matches the configured cluster list.
For an invalid destination, the helper removes only exact ResourcesFinalizerName and merge-patches changed finalizers; patch errors return.
The child index selects an ApplicationSet controller reference by expected apiVersion/kind and indexes its name.

A deleting ApplicationSet whose effective policy disallows deletion invokes owner-reference removal and returns its errors.
Owner-reference removal clears the entire owner list on each returned Application and updates it, returning list or update errors.
RollingSync step matching tests generated Application labels and records selected Application names.
The updateApp helper merges labels/annotations when merge is true and otherwise replaces both maps.
IsHydrateRequested treats every present hydrate annotation as a request and only exact hard as hard hydration.
PersistHydrationStatus removes the hydrate annotation while persisting hydration status.
Application summary collects link-prefix annotation values into a unique sorted URL list.
ValidateManagedByURL skips missing/empty values and reports InvalidSpecError when external-URL validation fails.
Manifest generation forwards the Application manifest-generate-paths annotation to the repository request.
A nonempty manifest-generate-paths annotation with a synced revision and zero repository depth selects path-specific revision updating.
Source refresh paths give a hydration sync source precedence, then split and trim annotation paths, discard empty entries and resolve root-relative or source-relative paths.
An empty changed-file or refresh-path list returns true; otherwise exact, descendant or filepath-pattern matching selects changed files.
Matching revision/repository sources use the path matcher, queue refresh with optional jitter, and otherwise can warm manifest-cache revision keys.
Application annotation constants define refresh/hydrate and manifest-generation paths.
IsRefreshRequested treats any present refresh annotation as a request; only exact hard selects hard refresh.
needRefreshAppStatus gives an explicit refresh request precedence over expiry and source/destination changes.
persistReconciliationStatus removes the refresh annotation while persisting updated status.
Application skip-reconcile parsing only stops processing on a successfully parsed true; invalid text logs and does not stop.
IsDeletionConfirmed rejects missing/invalid text and requires approval time at or after deletion start.
Application finalization rereads current state; missing destination cluster removes cascade and pre/post-delete tokens, while REST-config errors return.
Pre-delete hooks retain their finalizer until complete, then the controller patches its removal.
Cascade finalization checks approval/pending deletion, chooses propagation policy, deletes permitted resources, rereads remaining objects and removes the cascade token only when none remain.
Post-delete hooks retain their token while pending and remove it only after completion.
updateFinalizers merge-patches the Application metadata finalizers through its namespaced client.
Argo delete requires Application delete RBAC, calculates propagation finalizers and avoids adding a token after deletion starts.
The continuous producer removes stale provenance before authoring the exact qualifying immutable release path.
The health exception requires the exact marker and matching applied source; it does not treat the annotation as an execution receipt.
Bootstrap derives root/project identities and authors root labels and runtime namespace annotation.
Bootstrap ownership exemption checks identity, root label and project; other namespace claimants must match selected groups.
Preflight retrieves existing named Argo objects and rejects root-label conflicts or changed root repository/namespace claims.
The supported chart authors workload project identity, root label and project sync wave.
Each release-group Application has group identity, sync-wave/Helm-release annotations and a project label; spec.project selects its project.
The maintained platform bootstrap selects project sync wave -1.
The supported template selects group wave and serializes Helm releases as a JSON annotation.
Wave parses the annotation as an integer and falls back to Helm hook weight.
Hook weight parses its own integer annotation and otherwise returns zero.
Sync task ordering compares phase, wave, then kind before name.
The maintained SPIRE Application explicitly selects ServerSideDiff and platform health annotations.
Annotation options split comma-separated text, trim and deduplicate nonempty entries, then compare exact strings.
ServerSideDiff follows controller or true annotation; false annotation overrides both.
Parent health aggregation skips a live resource only for the exact ignore-healthcheck value true.
Platform bootstrap authors ignore-healthcheck=true and health-mode=observed for its child Applications.
The installed health script checks errors and failed operations before the observed-health branch.
The other health branch requires matching selected source, destination, revision and a successful operation.
GitOps preflight requires the installed annotation tracking mode and exact health customization.
Namespace claims parse the runtime namespace JSON annotation, validate its array/name contract and include the destination namespace.
Helm ownership prerequisites use bundle group release names, not an Application annotation.

receiverContract.changeImpact: The selected desired configuration joins project permission, repository rendering, target cluster/namespace and sync policy. Rendering must succeed before execution. Manual child Applications do not synchronize merely because their definitions are deployed; an automated root can deploy those definitions while their child operations remain unscheduled. Persisted comparison and operation state can suppress or resume synchronization.
crossFieldConditions: Argo Application Create validates/normalizes before Kubernetes Create and ignores a supplied operation by setting it nil. The full Argo Update helper replaces spec on the currently stored object and retries conflicts up to ten reads; it does not copy incoming status or operation into that stored object. These are Argo server endpoint contracts; direct Kubernetes writes have a separate admission and update contract.

Argo server validation resolves the destination and checks project permissions even when optional repository validation is disabled. With validation enabled, it validates the repository and rejects nonempty returned conditions. It then normalizes spec: empty project becomes default, an empty sync policy becomes nil, and empty selected source options are removed. Full UpdateSpec assigns the supplied complete spec before this path; omission inside that supplied spec is not a partial update.

Omission or null of spec in a fresh object leaves its value struct empty. A zero spec has no usable source or destination: ValidatePermissions reports invalid-source conditions and returns before destination checks when the source identity fails. Full Argo UpdateSpec replaces the complete spec; it is not a patch of omitted children. Direct Kubernetes declarative apply has its own admission and field-ownership semantics. Check the installed CRD and stored object before diagnosing a rejected write.

A nil sync policy or nil automated setting disables automatic sync. A present empty automated object enables it because enabled is nil, but prune, selfHeal and allowEmpty remain false. An empty sync policy is normalized to nil by the Argo API; direct Kubernetes storage need not run that endpoint normalization. Manual Sync starts with configured options/retry; a non-nil request options list replaces the complete list, including an empty list, and a non-nil request retry replaces the complete strategy. A running operation uses its stored settings.

Successful, non-dry-run, non-selective sync can append a history source/revision snapshot, bounded by revisionHistoryLimit (10 when omitted/null). History marshal or patch errors change the operation to OperationError after resource execution; they do not undo resources and can enter the configured failed/error retry path. Rollback requires retained history, no deletion in progress and automation disabled; it uses stored sources/revisions with current policy options. It reapplies manifests and is not restoration of database or volume data, deleted credentials or external service state.

ExplicitType rejects more than one present Helm/Kustomize/Directory/Plugin pointer; no pointer uses discovery. Disabled explicit generation falls back to Directory.

Path resolution and Helm failures stop manifest generation.

With validation enabled, it validates the repository and rejects nonempty returned conditions. It then normalizes spec: empty project becomes default, an empty sync policy becomes nil, and empty selected source options are removed. Full UpdateSpec assigns the supplied complete spec before this path; omission inside that supplied spec is not a partial update.

Before renderer selection, mergeSourceParameters applies repository source parameter files in order to a deep-copied source using JSON merge patch and typed unmarshal. Missing files/directories are skipped; read, YAML conversion, patch or decode errors stop selection. It restores chart, path, repoURL and targetRevision to the original source after these merges, then writes the resulting source back. ExplicitType rejects more than one present Helm/Kustomize/Directory/Plugin pointer; no pointer uses discovery. Disabled explicit generation falls back to Directory.

Full UpdateSpec assigns the supplied complete spec before this path; omission inside that supplied spec is not a partial update.

ExplicitType rejects more than one present Helm/Kustomize/Directory/Plugin pointer; no pointer uses discovery. Disabled explicit generation falls back to Directory.

The selected Helm release name overrides the application-name default only when nonempty. contract.description: ValuesObject specifies Helm values to be passed to helm template, defined as a map. This takes precedence over Values.

cases.name: omitted-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: The valuesObject pointer remains nil; ValuesYAML uses the values string.

cases.sourceOutcome: A fresh JSON null value makes the pointer nil. The optional valuesObject therefore does not override values.

cases.name: empty-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: A present {} allocates the extension and preserves raw JSON object bytes. ValuesYAML converts those bytes to YAML and uses them instead of values.

receiverContract.changeImpact: The repo server constructs Helm template options for this selected source. A nil Helm options pointer makes no Helm-specific overrides. It resolves ordered value files, writes inline values to one temporary file, assigns parameters to --set or --set-string, resolves file parameters, then invokes helm template. Later entries with the same parameter name overwrite earlier entries in the same parameter map. valuesObject takes precedence over values when its raw bytes are present. Path resolution and Helm failures stop manifest generation.
crossFieldConditions: When sourceHydrator is present, GetSource/GetSources use its sync source. Otherwise a nonempty sources list selects multi-source mode; source is used only without that list. Empty sources does not select multi-source mode. GetSource returns the first source in multi-source mode; GetSources retains all entries.

A Helm parameter item has name, value and forceString; an empty name is passed through to the Helm command rather than skipped by the repo-server loop. A file-parameter path must resolve within the supported source/path and URL schemes.

For a single manifest source, repoURL and path or chart are required. For a multi-source entry, repoURL and path, chart or ref are required. A chart requires nonempty targetRevision. Permission failures become InvalidSpecError conditions.

The controller renders sources in list order and appends their target objects in that order. Deduplication groups target objects by resource identity and retains the last target of each group, adding RepeatedResourceWarning for duplicates. This is manifest precedence, not independent synchronization of each source.

Argo Application Create validates/normalizes before Kubernetes Create and ignores a supplied operation by setting it nil. The full Argo Update helper replaces spec on the currently stored object and retries conflicts up to ten reads; it does not copy incoming status or operation into that stored object. These are Argo server endpoint contracts; direct Kubernetes writes have a separate admission and update contract.

Argo server validation resolves the destination and checks project permissions even when optional repository validation is disabled. With validation enabled, it validates the repository and rejects nonempty returned conditions. It then normalizes spec: empty project becomes default, an empty sync policy becomes nil, and empty selected source options are removed. Full UpdateSpec assigns the supplied complete spec before this path; omission inside that supplied spec is not a partial update.

Before renderer selection, mergeSourceParameters applies repository source parameter files in order to a deep-copied source using JSON merge patch and typed unmarshal. Missing files/directories are skipped; read, YAML conversion, patch or decode errors stop selection. It restores chart, path, repoURL and targetRevision to the original source after these merges, then writes the resulting source back. ExplicitType rejects more than one present Helm/Kustomize/Directory/Plugin pointer; no pointer uses discovery. Disabled explicit generation falls back to Directory.

Repository parameter override files are .argocd-source.yaml followed by .argocd-source-<application-name>.yaml when the name is nonempty. The later file has merge precedence. The final typed source is assigned back after restoring the four source identity fields.

The selected Helm release name overrides the application-name default only when nonempty. Helm namespace defaults to the selected destination namespace; cluster Kubernetes/API capabilities supply defaults when their source overrides are empty. Omitted skipTests, skipCrds, skipSchemaValidation and passCredentials are false. False skipCrds adds --include-crds; true skipTests adds --skip-tests; true skipSchemaValidation adds --skip-schema-validation. Omitting these fields does not disable CRD output or schema validation by this wrapper.

Wait is duration multiplied by factor to the retry count; a positive maximum caps it. Invalid duration returns an error.

contract.description: Options allow you to specify whole app sync-options

cases.condition: $.spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions is absent from a present immediate parent in a fresh typed object
cases.name: omitted-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: The field remains nil in a fresh parent. The named consumer conditions below decide whether that value supplies a fallback, skips work or fails.

cases.condition: $.spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions is JSON null in a present immediate parent
cases.name: null-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: JSON null sets this array to nil.

cases.condition: $.spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions has a present empty or primitive zero value
cases.name: empty-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: A present empty [] creates a non-nil array with zero entries. No element is removed from a different collection by this fresh decode.

cases.condition: The resource sync-options annotation contains whitespace, duplicates or conflicting key=value strings
cases.name: resource-annotation-parser
cases.sourceOutcome: GetAnnotationCSVs splits on commas, trims each token, removes empty tokens and duplicate exact tokens, and preserves first-occurrence order. HasAnnotationOption tests exact membership after that normalization. GetAnnotationOptionValue returns the first exact key= prefix match.

cases.condition: A cascaded Application deletion reads Delete=false or Delete=confirm from current spec options or live annotations.
cases.name: delete-finalization-option
cases.sourceOutcome: The live resource Delete value overrides the current spec fallback. Delete=false excludes it from cascade deletion; CRDs, self-referenced Applications and Helm keep-policy resources are also excluded. A stored resource confirmation flag without a sufficiently recent deletion-approved timestamp blocks deletion. Resource deletion errors return, and finalizer removal waits for eligible resources to disappear.

cases.condition: A prune or cascade delete needs confirmation.
cases.name: approval-time
cases.sourceOutcome: The Application deletion-approved annotation must parse as RFC3339 and be at or after the operation start for prune, or Application deletion timestamp for cascade. Missing, malformed or earlier time does not approve.

cases.condition: ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true.
cases.name: selective-diff-task-filter
cases.sourceOutcome: The engine filters both dry-run and pending execution tasks using resource diff results. It keeps hooks, missing live/target objects and unknown diff entries; it skips a nonhook task only when a known diff is unmodified and both target/live exist. The declared ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=false resource literal is not a disable branch in this filter.

cases.condition: Resource API discovery returns NotFound.
cases.name: missing-resource-dry-run
cases.sourceOutcome: The dry-run skip applies only for the app option, target annotation or a CRD of that group/kind in this sync. Other discovery errors become SyncFailed. Successful discovery still runs project permission validation. This option does not guarantee the later resource apply succeeds.

cases.condition: More than one recognized PrunePropagationPolicy literal is present.
cases.name: propagation-literal-conflict
cases.sourceOutcome: The fixed switch checks background first, then foreground, then orphan. List order does not choose this policy. With none, foreground remains the initial default.

cases.condition: A syncOptions string differs in case or whitespace from the exact evaluator literal
cases.name: exact-option
cases.sourceOutcome: HasOption uses slices.Contains. The different string does not activate that exact option. GetOptionValue returns the value of the first string with the exact key= prefix; it does not validate later conflicts.

cases.condition: FailOnSharedResource=true and the application has a shared-resource condition
cases.name: shared-resource-stop
cases.sourceOutcome: SyncAppState sets OperationFailed and returns before constructing the sync context. It does not start applying that operation.

cases.condition: ServerSideApply=true on the app or target resource, with optional target ServerSideApply=false
cases.name: ssa-resource-precedence
cases.sourceOutcome: A dry run disables SSA. Otherwise the target resource ServerSideApply=false disables it before the app/target true OR expression. Application ServerSideApply=false is not a global disable evaluator in this path.

cases.condition: SSA evaluates true, migration is enabled, this is not a dry run and the live resource has Update ownership for the selected CSA manager
cases.name: ownership-migration-before-replace

contract.description:
AppProject provides a logical grouping of applications, providing controls for:
* where the apps may deploy to (cluster whitelist)
* what may be deployed (repository whitelist, resource whitelist/blacklist)
* who can access these applications (roles, OIDC group claims bindings)
* and what they can do (RBAC policies)
* automation access to these roles (JWT tokens)

receiverContract.changeImpact: The selected project limits accepted source repositories, destination namespaces and resource group/kinds. These permissions are checked together and do not grant Kubernetes RBAC. A present orphan monitor adds observation and optional warnings, without deleting orphaned resources.
crossFieldConditions: Argo Project Create normalizes policies, validates and creates the provided project. On AlreadyExists without upsert, an equal spec returns the existing project and a different spec fails. With upsert it replaces only the existing spec before Update. Argo Project Update normalizes both policies and token lists, validates, obtains a project lock, checks cluster/repository permissions and submits the supplied whole project. It returns the API Update error; this endpoint body has no automatic conflict retry loop.

Omission or null of spec leaves its value struct empty. With no effective source/destination positive matches, deployment permission is denied; an omitted namespaced whitelist alone permits group/kinds but does not bypass destination authorization. An empty cluster whitelist permits no cluster resources. Global and project-scoped additions can alter these effective permissions.

The object can contain stored state and (Application only) an operation request. Persisted operation and history values have active resume, suppression and rollback roles. These state routes do not replace desired spec.

contract.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy is a Kubernetes third-party resource with an
modified version of CiliumNetworkPolicy which is cluster scoped rather than
namespace scoped.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: spec or specs must be provided

cases.condition: No resource request body is supplied.
cases.name: absent-request-body
cases.sourceOutcome: An absent object supplies no resource to the request boundary.

cases.condition: Fresh request decoding receives a JSON null body.
cases.name: null-request-body
cases.sourceOutcome: A null request value does not establish a valid Kubernetes resource. Parse requires an actual typed object with name and policy inputs.

cases.condition: The request body is an empty object {}.
cases.name: empty-request-object
cases.sourceOutcome: {} has neither a name nor desired rules. Parse returns the missing-name error first. API envelope and metadata validation precede this typed operation.

cases.condition: All four direction slices have zero length, including explicitly present empty arrays
cases.name: zero-direction-rule
cases.sourceOutcome: Sanitize returns the at-least-one-direction error. This is an actual Cilium 1.20.1 product restriction; the Rule comment that an omitted pair has no effect does not override the implementation.

cases.condition: spec and specs are both non-nil and all rules sanitize
cases.name: both-policy-inputs
cases.sourceOutcome: Parse returns spec first and then all specs items. A failure in any item prevents the agent from submitting the resulting object update.

cases.condition: spec is nil and specs is a present empty array after fresh decoding
cases.name: empty-rule-list
cases.sourceOutcome: Parse returns an empty Rules slice without the both-nil error. UpdatePolicy receives zero translated entries; this is not evidence that an API server accepted the request.

cases.condition: A specs array contains JSON null
cases.name: null-rule-item
cases.sourceOutcome: The Rules element type is *Rule. The nil item is retained, and Parse calls rule.Sanitize without a nil guard. This input can panic in the typed path; do not describe it as a sanitized no-op.

receiverContract.changeImpact: Parse appends spec and then every specs rule. Neither field overrides the other. Both nil returns an empty-policy error. A non-nil empty specs list passes that nil check and returns zero rules if spec is nil. A present empty rule fails Sanitize before import.
crossFieldConditions: A rule must contain at least one ingress, ingressDeny, egress or egressDeny item. A present direction field with [] satisfies a CRD presence alternative but does not satisfy the runtime length check. Cilium has no policyTypes field in these policy types; Kubernetes NetworkPolicy policyTypes defaults must not be applied here.

Prefix identity allocation precedes repository replacement. After startup the importer waits up to 10 seconds for IP-cache progress; timeout warns about possible drops and continues, rather than proving safe enforcement or rejecting the policy. Repository DoneChan reports insertion revision before endpoint regeneration.

Policy import is asynchronous: submitting UpdatePolicy is not proof of endpoint or datapath enforcement. Parse failure stops the new submission. Deletion submits the same resource identity with no rules and clears reference/cache indices.

The importer owns a buffered update channel and processes buffered batches through one observer. UpdatePolicy sends directly to that channel; the function has no context, error return or queue-full timeout, so it can block waiting for queue space. ReplaceByResource holds the repository write lock across old-rule removal, replacement insertion, selector release and revision increment. Replacing the same resource does not accumulate its old rules, but repeated replacements can increment the revision. A failed Parse sends no replacement, so it does not by itself remove rules already imported for that resource. Correct the authored rule before retrying, and check the repository/endpoint observations separately.

Within a batch, repository replacement and DoneChan revision reporting precede endpoint computation and regeneration. A monitor notification error is logged after replacement and does not roll back that replacement. Endpoint updates and stale-prefix cleanup follow. The importer does not return a behavioral failure from processUpdates; nil is not proof that every downstream endpoint, proxy or datapath operation succeeded. The agent/network operator owns diagnosis after insertion.

Parse requires a name, rejects both nil spec fields, sanitizes each rule, translates spec first and each specs item afterwards. It returns on the first invalid rule.
The agent calls Parse before RulesToPolicyEntries and UpdatePolicy; a parse error returns before sending a policy update.
Rule.Sanitize rejects zero total direction items, requires exactly one non-nil subject selector and sanitizes each direction.
Sanitize validates subject and directions before translating a rule.
Ingress allow entries retain subject, direction, labels, default posture, peers, ports, authentication and log.
ReplaceByResource removes the old resource rules, inserts replacements, collects affected subjects and bumps the repository revision.
UpdatePolicy queues the update.
The importer allocates prefix identities before replacing resource rules and reports a repository revision before endpoint regeneration.
After repository updates it triggers endpoint computation/regeneration and prunes stale prefix metadata.
After startup, prefix allocation waits up to 10 seconds; timeout logs a warning and policy import continues.
The importer creates a buffered channel, batches it through an observer and UpdatePolicy performs a direct send.
ReplaceByResource holds its write lock, removes old resource rules, inserts replacements, releases selectors and increments revision.
Insertion revision reporting precedes logged monitor errors, endpoint updates and stale-prefix cleanup.
Delete removes resource rules and clears service and raw-policy caches.
Delete submits a no-rules PolicyUpdate under the resource identity.

For these normal-tier Cilium policies, matching deny rules take precedence over matching allow rules. Deny rules have ports and ICMP fields but no L7 or authentication fields. Effective policy also includes other selecting policies, daemon enforcement mode and host-firewall settings.

Ingress common-rule sanitization rejects two nonempty families among endpoints, nodes, entities, direct CIDRs, CIDR sets and groups. Egress counts the corresponding authored families plus services; generated endpoint/CIDR-set entries are excluded. Allow egress adds toFQDNs to that count separately. These checks compare lengths, not whether an empty slice is nil. Items provide alternative peers; requirements inside one selector are combined.

mergeEndpointSelectors returns nil immediately if any endpoint, node, entity, direct-CIDR or CIDR-set slice is non-nil with zero entries. It does this before appending any other peer family. Omission or null leaves an ordinary slice nil, while [] can discard even a different nonempty family that passed the length-based checks. Empty FQDN and group slices do not themselves trigger this early return. The L4 constructor converts a zero-length L3 result to wildcard peers. This can widen an allow entry or broaden a deny entry; it does not bypass its remaining L4, subject or direction conditions. This consequence is a source inference, with no traffic run.

Policy authors should omit unused peer arrays instead of adding explicit [] beside an intended nonempty peer family. The network-policy maintainer owns review of the sanitizer/translation mismatch. The safe boundary is the current nil/empty distinction; proving a corrected or supported mixed-family behavior requires a matching source change and bounded policy-map/traffic checks. The code comment describes an expectation about one selector family, but it does not override the length check or prove the historical reason for this cross-field result.

contract.description:
EgressRule contains all rule types which can be applied at egress, i.e.
network traffic that originates inside the endpoint and exits the endpoint
selected by the endpointSelector.

  - All members of this structure are optional. If omitted or empty, the
    member will have no effect on the rule.

  - If multiple members of the structure are specified, then all members
    must match in order for the rule to take effect.

  - ToEndpoints, ToCIDR, ToCIDRSet, ToEntities, ToServices and ToGroups are
    mutually exclusive. Only one of these members may be present within an
    individual rule.

cases.condition: $.spec.egress[] is absent from a present immediate parent in a fresh object
cases.name: omitted-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: No element exists at this position. It does not contribute a zero element.

cases.condition: $.spec.egress[] is JSON null within a present immediate parent
cases.name: null-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: Null has no effect on an ordinary struct. A custom decoder named below can change the result. The slice retains this position, with a nil pointer, primitive zero or zero struct as applicable.

cases.condition: $.spec.egress[] is a present empty collection/object or primitive zero
cases.name: empty-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: The explicit empty or zero value remains the zero struct; it is not an omitted field.

cases.condition: The same resource already has imported rules and a replacement object fails Parse
cases.name: parse-failure-preserves-prior-import
cases.sourceOutcome: The watcher returns before UpdatePolicy, so this failed submission makes no repository replacement. It does not by itself delete previously imported rules. This describes the submission path, not every later selecting-policy or endpoint-state change.

cases.condition: Repository replacement succeeds but SendEvent for its monitor notification returns an error
cases.name: monitor-notification-failure-after-import
cases.sourceOutcome: The importer logs that error and continues endpoint-update processing and stale-prefix cleanup. It does not undo the repository replacement or report the monitor failure through DoneChan.

cases.condition: A direction is [] versus [{}]
cases.name: empty-direction-vs-item
cases.sourceOutcome: [] contributes no direction item and no directional entry. [{}] contributes one entry with empty peers and ports; the L4 constructor expands empty peers to wildcard. That entry can allow all or deny all in its direction, according to its parent allow/deny field.

cases.condition: An ingress item has fromEndpoints:[] and a valid nonempty fromCIDR, or the corresponding checked empty slice and nonempty family on an egress/deny entry
cases.name: explicit-empty-peer-discards-other-family
cases.sourceOutcome: The common length check does not reject a zero-length family beside one nonempty family. Translation returns nil before adding that other family. L4 creates wildcard L3 peers while retaining the entry verdict, ports and subject. Omitted/null fromEndpoints does not trigger this short circuit.

cases.condition: The groups slice, or allow-egress toFQDNs slice, is explicitly [] beside one valid nonempty peer family, and all other checked slices are nil
cases.name: empty-unchecked-peer-family
cases.sourceOutcome: The empty group/FQDN slice does not trigger mergeEndpointSelectors early return; the other family can reach the appended L3 selectors. This is different from an explicit empty endpoint/node/entity/CIDR/CIDR-set slice.

receiverContract.changeImpact: The field participates in the policy object consumed by Parse. The watcher imports the complete translated rule set under the resource identity; it does not apply an isolated leaf update. The egress direction applies to traffic leaving the selected subject. Its entries have Allow verdicts. The opposite direction is evaluated independently; an end-to-end connection can require both source egress and destination ingress permission.
crossFieldConditions: Prefix identity allocation precedes repository replacement. After startup the importer waits up to 10 seconds for IP-cache progress; timeout warns about possible drops and continues, rather than proving safe enforcement or rejecting the policy. Repository DoneChan reports insertion revision before endpoint regeneration.

Policy import is asynchronous: submitting UpdatePolicy is not proof of endpoint or datapath enforcement. Parse failure stops the new submission. Deletion submits the same resource identity with no rules and clears reference/cache indices.

The importer owns a buffered update channel and processes buffered batches through one observer. UpdatePolicy sends directly to that channel; the function has no context, error return or queue-full timeout, so it can block waiting for queue space. ReplaceByResource holds the repository write lock across old-rule removal, replacement insertion, selector release and revision increment. Replacing the same resource does not accumulate its old rules, but repeated replacements can increment the revision. A failed Parse sends no replacement, so it does not by itself remove rules already imported for that resource. Correct the authored rule before retrying, and check the repository/endpoint observations separately.

Within a batch, repository replacement and DoneChan revision reporting precede endpoint computation and regeneration. A monitor notification error is logged after replacement and does not roll back that replacement. Endpoint updates and stale-prefix cleanup follow. The importer does not return a behavioral failure from processUpdates; nil is not proof that every downstream endpoint, proxy or datapath operation succeeded. The agent/network operator owns diagnosis after insertion.

For these normal-tier Cilium policies, matching deny rules take precedence over matching allow rules. Deny rules have ports and ICMP fields but no L7 or authentication fields. Effective policy also includes other selecting policies, daemon enforcement mode and host-firewall settings.

Ingress common-rule sanitization rejects two nonempty families among endpoints, nodes, entities, direct CIDRs, CIDR sets and groups. Egress counts the corresponding authored families plus services; generated endpoint/CIDR-set entries are excluded. Allow egress adds toFQDNs to that count separately. These checks compare lengths, not whether an empty slice is nil. Items provide alternative peers; requirements inside one selector are combined.

mergeEndpointSelectors returns nil immediately if any endpoint, node, entity, direct-CIDR or CIDR-set slice is non-nil with zero entries. It does this before appending any other peer family. Omission or null leaves an ordinary slice nil, while [] can discard even a different nonempty family that passed the length-based checks. Empty FQDN and group slices do not themselves trigger this early return. The L4 constructor converts a zero-length L3 result to wildcard peers. This can widen an allow entry or broaden a deny entry; it does not bypass its remaining L4, subject or direction conditions. This consequence is a source inference, with no traffic run.

Policy authors should omit unused peer arrays instead of adding explicit [] beside an intended nonempty peer family. The network-policy maintainer owns review of the sanitizer/translation mismatch. The safe boundary is the current nil/empty distinction; proving a corrected or supported mixed-family behavior requires a matching source change and bounded policy-map/traffic checks. contract.description:
ToEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an EndpointSelector to
which the endpoints subject to the rule are allowed to communicate.

Example:
Any endpoint with the label "role=frontend" can communicate with any
endpoint carrying the label "role=backend".

Note that while an empty non-nil ToEndpoints does not select anything,
nil ToEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts
are also specified.
To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.

contract.description:

flag to be set. These protocols do not use transport-layer ports.

Named port specified for a container may narrow this down, but may not
contradict this.

contract.description:
EnableDefaultDeny determines whether this policy configures the
subject endpoint(s) to have a default deny mode. If enabled,
this causes all traffic not explicitly allowed by a network policy
to be dropped.

If not specified, the default is true for each traffic direction
that has rules, and false otherwise. For example, if a policy
only has Ingress or IngressDeny rules, then the default for
ingress is true and egress is false.

If multiple policies apply to an endpoint, that endpoint's default deny
will be enabled if any policy requests it.

This is useful for creating broad-based network policies that will not
cause endpoints to enter default-deny mode.

Ingress common-rule sanitization rejects two nonempty families among endpoints, nodes, entities, direct CIDRs, CIDR sets and groups. Egress counts the corresponding authored families plus services; generated endpoint/CIDR-set entries are excluded. Allow egress adds toFQDNs to that count separately. mergeEndpointSelectors returns nil immediately if any endpoint, node, entity, direct-CIDR or CIDR-set slice is non-nil with zero entries. It does this before appending any other peer family. This can widen an allow entry or broaden a deny entry; it does not bypass its remaining L4, subject or direction conditions. This consequence is a source inference, with no traffic run.

The safe boundary is the current nil/empty distinction; proving a corrected or supported mixed-family behavior requires a matching source change and bounded policy-map/traffic checks. The code comment describes an expectation about one selector family, but it does not override the length check or prove the historical reason for this cross-field result.

contract.description:
EgressRule contains all rule types which can be applied at egress, i.e.
network traffic that originates inside the endpoint and exits the endpoint
selected by the endpointSelector.

  - All members of this structure are optional. If omitted or empty, the
    member will have no effect on the rule.

  - If multiple members of the structure are specified, then all members
    must match in order for the rule to take effect.

  - ToEndpoints, ToCIDR, ToCIDRSet, ToEntities, ToServices and ToGroups are
    mutually exclusive. Only one of these members may be present within an
    individual rule.

cases.condition: $.spec.egress[] is absent from a present immediate parent in a fresh object
cases.name: omitted-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: No element exists at this position. It does not contribute a zero element.

cases.condition: $.spec.egress[] is JSON null within a present immediate parent
cases.name: null-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: Null has no effect on an ordinary struct. A custom decoder named below can change the result. The slice retains this position, with a nil pointer, primitive zero or zero struct as applicable.

cases.condition: $.spec.egress[] is a present empty collection/object or primitive zero
cases.name: empty-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: The explicit empty or zero value remains the zero struct; it is not an omitted field.

cases.condition: The same resource already has imported rules and a replacement object fails Parse
cases.name: parse-failure-preserves-prior-import
cases.sourceOutcome: The watcher returns before UpdatePolicy, so this failed submission makes no repository replacement. It does not by itself delete previously imported rules. This describes the submission path, not every later selecting-policy or endpoint-state change.

cases.condition: Repository replacement succeeds but SendEvent for its monitor notification returns an error
cases.name: monitor-notification-failure-after-import
cases.sourceOutcome: The importer logs that error and continues endpoint-update processing and stale-prefix cleanup. It does not undo the repository replacement or report the monitor failure through DoneChan.

cases.condition: A direction is [] versus [{}]
cases.name: empty-direction-vs-item
cases.sourceOutcome: [] contributes no direction item and no directional entry. [{}] contributes one entry with empty peers and ports; the L4 constructor expands empty peers to wildcard. That entry can allow all or deny all in its direction, according to its parent allow/deny field.

cases.condition: An ingress item has fromEndpoints:[] and a valid nonempty fromCIDR, or the corresponding checked empty slice and nonempty family on an egress/deny entry
cases.name: explicit-empty-peer-discards-other-family
cases.sourceOutcome: The common length check does not reject a zero-length family beside one nonempty family. Translation returns nil before adding that other family. L4 creates wildcard L3 peers while retaining the entry verdict, ports and subject. Omitted/null fromEndpoints does not trigger this short circuit.

cases.condition: The groups slice, or allow-egress toFQDNs slice, is explicitly [] beside one valid nonempty peer family, and all other checked slices are nil
cases.name: empty-unchecked-peer-family
cases.sourceOutcome: The empty group/FQDN slice does not trigger mergeEndpointSelectors early return; the other family can reach the appended L3 selectors. This is different from an explicit empty endpoint/node/entity/CIDR/CIDR-set slice.

crossFieldConditions: Prefix identity allocation precedes repository replacement. After startup the importer waits up to 10 seconds for IP-cache progress; timeout warns about possible drops and continues, rather than proving safe enforcement or rejecting the policy. Repository DoneChan reports insertion revision before endpoint regeneration.

Policy import is asynchronous: submitting UpdatePolicy is not proof of endpoint or datapath enforcement. Parse failure stops the new submission. Deletion submits the same resource identity with no rules and clears reference/cache indices.

The importer owns a buffered update channel and processes buffered batches through one observer. UpdatePolicy sends directly to that channel; the function has no context, error return or queue-full timeout, so it can block waiting for queue space. ReplaceByResource holds the repository write lock across old-rule removal, replacement insertion, selector release and revision increment. Replacing the same resource does not accumulate its old rules, but repeated replacements can increment the revision. A failed Parse sends no replacement, so it does not by itself remove rules already imported for that resource. Correct the authored rule before retrying, and check the repository/endpoint observations separately.

Within a batch, repository replacement and DoneChan revision reporting precede endpoint computation and regeneration. A monitor notification error is logged after replacement and does not roll back that replacement. Endpoint updates and stale-prefix cleanup follow. The importer does not return a behavioral failure from processUpdates; nil is not proof that every downstream endpoint, proxy or datapath operation succeeded. For these normal-tier Cilium policies, matching deny rules take precedence over matching allow rules. Deny rules have ports and ICMP fields but no L7 or authentication fields. Effective policy also includes other selecting policies, daemon enforcement mode and host-firewall settings.

Ingress common-rule sanitization rejects two nonempty families among endpoints, nodes, entities, direct CIDRs, CIDR sets and groups. Egress counts the corresponding authored families plus services; generated endpoint/CIDR-set entries are excluded. Allow egress adds toFQDNs to that count separately. These checks compare lengths, not whether an empty slice is nil. Items provide alternative peers; requirements inside one selector are combined.

mergeEndpointSelectors returns nil immediately if any endpoint, node, entity, direct-CIDR or CIDR-set slice is non-nil with zero entries. It does this before appending any other peer family. Omission or null leaves an ordinary slice nil, while [] can discard even a different nonempty family that passed the length-based checks. Empty FQDN and group slices do not themselves trigger this early return. The L4 constructor converts a zero-length L3 result to wildcard peers. contract.description:
ToEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an EndpointSelector to
which the endpoints subject to the rule are allowed to communicate.

Example:
Any endpoint with the label "role=frontend" can communicate with any
endpoint carrying the label "role=backend".

Note that while an empty non-nil ToEndpoints does not select anything,
nil ToEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts
are also specified.
To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.

contract.description:
EnableDefaultDeny determines whether this policy configures the
subject endpoint(s) to have a default deny mode. If enabled,
this causes all traffic not explicitly allowed by a network policy
to be dropped.

If not specified, the default is true for each traffic direction
that has rules, and false otherwise. For example, if a policy
only has Ingress or IngressDeny rules, then the default for
ingress is true and egress is false.

If multiple policies apply to an endpoint, that endpoint's default deny
will be enabled if any policy requests it.

This is useful for creating broad-based network policies that will not
cause endpoints to enter default-deny mode.

cases.sourceOutcome: Null sets the slice to nil.

cases.name: empty-in-present-parent
cases.sourceOutcome: A present empty [] creates a non-nil slice with zero entries. This is a container value, not an empty item or key.

cases.condition: A direction is [] versus [{}]
cases.name: empty-direction-vs-item
cases.sourceOutcome: [] contributes no direction item and no directional entry. [{}] contributes one entry with empty peers and ports; the L4 constructor expands empty peers to wildcard. That entry can allow all or deny all in its direction, according to its parent allow/deny field.

receiverContract.changeImpact: The field participates in the policy object consumed by Parse. The watcher imports the complete translated rule set under the resource identity; it does not apply an isolated leaf update. The ingress direction applies to traffic entering the selected subject. Its entries have Allow verdicts. The opposite direction is evaluated independently; an end-to-end connection can require both source egress and destination ingress permission. Port rules constrain transport ports, protocols and optional proxy processing. Numeric/named port parsing and feature checks occur before filter construction. Named ports are resolved from endpoint identity metadata; an unresolved name is not a numeric zero wildcard.
crossFieldConditions: Prefix identity allocation precedes repository replacement. After startup the importer waits up to 10 seconds for IP-cache progress; timeout warns about possible drops and continues, rather than proving safe enforcement or rejecting the policy. Repository DoneChan reports insertion revision before endpoint regeneration.

Policy import is asynchronous: submitting UpdatePolicy is not proof of endpoint or datapath enforcement. Parse failure stops the new submission. Deletion submits the same resource identity with no rules and clears reference/cache indices.

The importer owns a buffered update channel and processes buffered batches through one observer. UpdatePolicy sends directly to that channel; the function has no context, error return or queue-full timeout, so it can block waiting for queue space. ReplaceByResource holds the repository write lock across old-rule removal, replacement insertion, selector release and revision increment. Replacing the same resource does not accumulate its old rules, but repeated replacements can increment the revision. A failed Parse sends no replacement, so it does not by itself remove rules already imported for that resource. Correct the authored rule before retrying, and check the repository/endpoint observations separately.

Within a batch, repository replacement and DoneChan revision reporting precede endpoint computation and regeneration. A monitor notification error is logged after replacement and does not roll back that replacement. Endpoint updates and stale-prefix cleanup follow. The importer does not return a behavioral failure from processUpdates; nil is not proof that every downstream endpoint, proxy or datapath operation succeeded. The agent/network operator owns diagnosis after insertion.

For these normal-tier Cilium policies, matching deny rules take precedence over matching allow rules. Deny rules have ports and ICMP fields but no L7 or authentication fields. Effective policy also includes other selecting policies, daemon enforcement mode and host-firewall settings.

A PortRule allows at most 40 port entries. A missing/empty ports collection is distinct from a port item with an empty port string. Omitted/empty protocol becomes ANY in typed Sanitize. In the numeric branch, the extended-protocol check compares the original exact-case protocol before ParseL4Proto uppercases it. Port text other than exactly "0" is rejected when that original protocol is an extended constant. Thus typed port:"80", protocol:"GRE" is rejected but protocol:"gre" bypasses that check before normalizing to GRE. Named ports take the earlier service-name branch and bypass this numeric check. Lowercase rejection by the CRD enum is a separate earlier API boundary. An empty port string requires EnableExtendedIPProtocols; numeric "0" does not take that empty-string gate. These branches do not establish a universal feature gate.

For numeric nonzero ports, an endPort greater than port expands a range in keysForRange. Zero, equal or lower endPort uses a single key; the typed sanitizer does not universally reject a lower endPort. Negative or over-65535 endPort remains an earlier CRD range error. Named port plus endPort has no general typed rejection. Initial ingress map construction resolves the name and then passes the resolved number and EndPort to keysForRange. Initial egress and incremental named-port selector updates instead create single-port keys. This source-derived asymmetry does not establish supported named ranges or a safe universal rejection. Policy authors should use numeric ranges or separate named single ports; the network-policy maintainer owns qualification of named ranges across initial and incremental paths before promising them.

receiverContract.changeImpact: The field participates in the policy object consumed by Parse. The watcher imports the complete translated rule set under the resource identity; it does not apply an isolated leaf update. The ingress direction applies to traffic entering the selected subject. crossFieldConditions: Prefix identity allocation precedes repository replacement. After startup the importer waits up to 10 seconds for IP-cache progress; timeout warns about possible drops and continues, rather than proving safe enforcement or rejecting the policy. Repository DoneChan reports insertion revision before endpoint regeneration.

Policy import is asynchronous: submitting UpdatePolicy is not proof of endpoint or datapath enforcement. Parse failure stops the new submission. Deletion submits the same resource identity with no rules and clears reference/cache indices.

The importer owns a buffered update channel and processes buffered batches through one observer. UpdatePolicy sends directly to that channel; the function has no context, error return or queue-full timeout, so it can block waiting for queue space. ReplaceByResource holds the repository write lock across old-rule removal, replacement insertion, selector release and revision increment. Port text other than exactly "0" is rejected when that original protocol is an extended constant. Thus typed port:"80", protocol:"GRE" is rejected but protocol:"gre" bypasses that check before normalizing to GRE. Named ports take the earlier service-name branch and bypass this numeric check. Lowercase rejection by the CRD enum is a separate earlier API boundary. An empty port string requires EnableExtendedIPProtocols; numeric "0" does not take that empty-string gate. These branches do not establish a universal feature gate.

For numeric nonzero ports, an endPort greater than port expands a range in keysForRange. contract.description:
Protocol is the L4 protocol. If "ANY", omitted or empty, any protocols
with transport ports (TCP, UDP, SCTP) match.

Accepted values: "TCP", "UDP", "SCTP", "VRRP", "IGMP", "GRE", "IPIP",
"IPV6", "ESP", "AH", "ANY"

Tunnel/encapsulation protocols (GRE, IPIP, IPV6, ESP, AH) and other
extended IP protocols (VRRP, IGMP) require the --enable-extended-ip-protocols
flag to be set. These protocols do not use transport-layer ports.

Matching on ICMP is not supported.

Named port specified for a container may narrow this down, but may not
contradict this.

contract.description: ingressClassName is the name of an IngressClass cluster resource. Ingress controller implementations use this field to know whether they should be serving this Ingress resource, by a transitive connection (controller -> IngressClass -> Ingress resource). Although the `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation (simple constant name) was never formally defined, it was widely supported by Ingress controllers to create a direct binding between Ingress controller and Ingress resources. Newly created Ingress resources should prefer using the field. However, even though the annotation is officially deprecated, for backwards compatibility reasons, ingress controllers should still honor that annotation if present.

podSelector is a label selector which selects pods. This field follows standard label selector semantics; if present but empty, it selects all pods.

If namespaceSelector is also set, then the NetworkPolicyPeer as a whole selects the pods matching podSelector in the Namespaces selected by NamespaceSelector. Otherwise it selects the pods matching podSelector in the policy's own namespace.

The ConfigMap volume plugin fetches the named object in the Pod namespace. Only optional NotFound becomes an empty object; other fetch failures fail setup. Payload is published by AtomicWriter; failure invokes deferred volume cleanup and success marks setup complete.

ConfigMap manager Get performs an API GET for each read. Cache uses a one-minute default TTL with a Node TTL override; first/new Pod references add a cache reference, and removing the last reference drops the item. Watch supplies a local list/watch result and stops watching after observing immutable:true. No manager changes an application environment or guarantees a refresh deadline.

Projected ConfigMap volumes also fetch in the Pod namespace, allow optional NotFound and use ConfigMap MakePayload. Payload contains both text and binary bags for an unfiltered mount; selected absent keys fail unless optional. Publication and application reads remain separate.

A mutable API update does not itself refresh a container. The selected Kubelet manager can use direct GET, a TTL cache or a watch cache. Volume setup and application reads are separate steps; no fixed end-to-end refresh deadline is established.

A Linux subPath mount binds the opened, resolved file. Inference from this mount path: replacing the parent volume symbolic link does not retarget the existing bind mount. Recreate the consumer mount through its workload procedure when new content is required.

The ConfigMap volume plugin fetches the named object in the Pod namespace. Only optional NotFound becomes an empty object; other fetch failures fail setup. Payload is published by AtomicWriter; failure invokes deferred volume cleanup and success marks setup complete.

ConfigMap manager Get performs an API GET for each read. Cache uses a one-minute default TTL with a Node TTL override; first/new Pod references add a cache reference, and removing the last reference drops the item. Watch supplies a local list/watch result and stops watching after observing immutable:true. No manager changes an application environment or guarantees a refresh deadline.

Projected ConfigMap volumes also fetch in the Pod namespace, allow optional NotFound and use ConfigMap MakePayload. Payload contains both text and binary bags for an unfiltered mount; selected absent keys fail unless optional. Publication and application reads remain separate.
