crossFieldConditions: A reference does not grant access or prove an owner exists. GC identity includes the actual owner UID; reusing a name with a new UID leaves the old reference dangling.
A namespaced owner must be in the dependent namespace; a cluster-scoped dependent cannot use a namespaced owner. This reference has no namespace override.
Only one true controller reference is allowed. controller does not determine whether a reference is an ownership edge; other owners also prevent collection while solid.

With OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement enabled, changing references after creation requires delete permission on the dependent. New blockOwnerDeletion:true requires update permission on mapped owner finalizers, or the wildcard finalizers grant. Mapping/authorization failures reject admission; the comment mentioning owner delete permission is not the exact authorization record.

GC operates from an informer-built graph but rereads objects and checks UID before destructive actions. A solid owner retains a dependent; no solid owner permits GC. Foreground waits only for blocking dependents known to that graph.

Mapping/GET/patch/delete errors can postpone GC and be rate-limited for retry; invalid cluster-to-namespace ownership is forgotten by the delete worker rather than fixed by repeated retries. Check scope, coordinates and the fresh UID before repairing a reference.

Orphan deletion uses a snapshot of dependents known to the GC graph. The worker patches those dependents concurrently to remove the selected owner UID; its strategic patch includes the dependent UID as a precondition. NotFound is tolerated. Other failures can leave only some dependents changed and retain the owner orphan finalizer. The worker retries with rate limiting and removes that token only after dependent patching succeeds; a failed token update also retries. This sequence does not delete the dependent workloads or prove that every external resource is inventoried.
This dependent is namespaced. A namespaced owner is looked up in this dependent namespace; cluster-scoped owners are resolved without a namespace.

managedFields records field ownership, not authentication or permission. The fieldManager request option (or user-agent fallback on non-apply requests), operation, endpoint version and subresource generate manager data; manually writing a manager name grants no access.

Non-apply root update distinguishes nil/omission from [] or [{}]: nil/empty decoded ownership falls back to the live object. Typed [] and a single zero entry select reset. With an existing live UID and empty ownership, the installed skip wrapper returns without tracking this update. Default create tracking probability is 1. A later Apply first records existing fields under before-first-apply. A subresource uses live ownership instead of request entries. CRD full-body coercion omits an empty [] before this selection; [{}] survives.

The metadata validator allows empty fieldsType, but DecodeManagedFields requires FieldsV1 and a nonempty apiVersion. A raw FieldsV1 token can decode without being a valid field trie. Update falls back to live ownership on decode failure; UpdateNoErrors clears ownership on later internal failure. Apply reports live-ownership decode errors and conflicts.

BuildManagerIdentifier excludes fieldsType, fieldsV1 and time. Update identity retains apiVersion; Apply identity removes apiVersion. manager, operation and subresource remain. The encoded versioned field set still retains its apiVersion.

The installed Apply version wrapper requires the full endpoint group/version/kind. Structured merge disallows nonnil authored managedFields. Request force is passed inward, but the exact manager kubectl has a last-applied migration exception: after conflicts, a nonempty valid same-version last-applied annotation permits an internal force=true retry only when all conflicting paths are covered and still equal their live values. Missing, malformed, wrong-version or unconvertible annotation leaves the original conflict. Partially covered conflicts return only the uncovered conflicts, without a forced retry. Resolve a conflict by inspecting the current fields and managers and changing ownership intent; force transfers conflicting ownership and can change another manager’s fields.

StripMeta removes apiVersion, kind, the metadata container path, and metadata name, namespace, creationTimestamp, selfLink, uid, clusterName, generation, managedFields and resourceVersion from the current manager field set; this is ownership exclusion, not removal from the stored object. Labels, annotations, finalizers and owners are not in this strip list. Update timestamps change when current-operation fields are recorded; an unchanged Apply preserves its prior manager time. Capping sorts Update entries by time then manager key and merges same-version entries into ancient-changes buckets. Apply entries are not capped. Distinct version buckets can prevent reducing the total to the configured cap of 10.

Successful exact kubectl Apply refreshes an existing nonempty kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation from a copied apply object without that annotation. Other managers and absent/empty annotations skip this update; encoding or setting failures return errors.

Strategy reset-field filters exclude fields that preparation restores; the status field-manager identity is distinct through subresource. Read the response after reset or conflict recovery. Do not assume a cleared managedFields list means apply succeeded or that all future conflicts disappear.

These are typed built-ins. Fresh null decodes managedFields to nil; [] remains a nonnil empty slice and [{}] remains one zero entry. Root non-apply field management selects reset for []/[{}], while omission/null falls back to live ownership. With a live UID and empty ownership, the installed skip wrapper skips tracking; reset does not immediately record the replacing manager. On create, the default wrapper tracks with probability 1. ConfigMap has no status or finalize REST route.

Deletion is a DELETE operation with DeleteOptions; writing timestamps or grace values in metadata is not a replacement for DELETE. Root create wipes those fields. Update preserves existing nonzero deletion time and fills absent old grace; immutable validation rejects an effective change that survives preparation.

Explicit propagation options override existing GC tokens and resource defaults. Foreground adds foregroundDeletion; orphan adds orphan; background removes those GC tokens. Other finalizers remain. GC unsupported/disabled branches do not install tokens that cannot be handled.

A DELETE response can mean deletion is pending. Pending finalizers retain the object with deletionTimestamp and zero grace for non-graceful resources. No new token may be added after stored deletion begins. Removing the last token can trigger delete during update when the old stored grace is absent or zero; this predicate does not compare a wall-clock deadline.

Retain finalizers until the responsible controller completes cleanup. Read fresh object UID, deletionTimestamp, finalizers and dependent state after timeout or partial failure. A missing object/new UID is a different lifetime; do not remove another lifetime’s finalizer. Check the external cleanup before manually removing a stuck token.

Orphan deletion uses a snapshot of dependents known to the GC graph. The worker patches those dependents concurrently to remove the selected owner UID; its strategic patch includes the dependent UID as a precondition. NotFound is tolerated. Other failures can leave only some dependents changed and retain the owner orphan finalizer. The worker retries with rate limiting and removes that token only after dependent patching succeeds; a failed token update also retries. This sequence does not delete the dependent workloads or prove that every external resource is inventoried.

ConfigMap, PVC and Service use ordinary non-graceful resource strategies: metadata grace does not select a Pod-like termination interval. Namespace has a separate DELETE implementation and two finalizer lists. Its first DELETE checks UID/version, stores Terminating and deletionTimestamp, and returns pending; later removal requires empty spec.finalizers as well as generic metadata-finalizer checks.

evidence.claim: Create requires a generated or explicit name and runs shared metadata checks.
Shared metadata validates scope, nonnegative generation, labels, annotations, ownership, finalizers and managed fields.
Owner-reference validation requires nonempty version/kind/name/UID, disallows v1 Event owners and permits at most one true controller pointer.
When OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement is enabled, changed references on non-create operations require delete permission on the dependent; unchanged and whitelisted requests bypass this check.
New blocking owner references require finalizers authorization; an update-finalizers wildcard grant bypasses REST mapping, otherwise every mapped owner is authorized.
Owner mapping requests update on the owner finalizers subresource; a namespaced owner uses the dependent namespace.
GC resolves the owner type and scope, rejects a namespaced owner of a cluster-dependent, fetches in the dependent namespace and treats NotFound or UID mismatch as dangling.
GC rereads the dependent, checks its UID, handles deleting owners and classifies the current owner references before deletion.
A solid owner prevents collection; dangling/waiting refs can be removed. Waiting-owner cycles can unblock references; no solid owner selects orphan, foreground or background deletion.
blockingDependents selects graph edges to this owner UID whose blockOwnerDeletion pointer is true.
Foreground GC retains the owner token while blocking dependents remain; otherwise it removes its foreground token.
Delete worker forgets stale virtual items and invalid cluster-to-namespace ownership, and returns retry for other errors including mapping failures.
The graph tracks current owner references and updates dependent edges when references are added, removed or changed.
Orphaning patches graph-known dependents concurrently, supplies dependent UID in the strategic patch and tolerates NotFound.
The orphan operation waits for all dependent attempts and returns aggregated non-NotFound failures.
The orphan worker forgets completed items and rate-limits retries for failed work.
The worker snapshots graph dependents and removes the owner orphan finalizer only after dependent patching succeeds; finalizer update failure also retries.
The default Update-manager cap is 10 and default create tracking probability is 1.
NewDefaultFieldManager installs version checking, last-applied updating/migration, skip-non-applied, manager capping, manager identity, time updating and metadata stripping wrappers.
Empty ownership on an existing live UID skips non-apply tracking; create tracking uses the configured probability.
Apply with empty ownership first records live fields under before-first-apply and returns bootstrap errors.
Apply rejects a full group/version/kind different from the configured endpoint.
Only exact kubectl handles merge conflicts through last-applied eligibility; complete coverage retries with force true and partial coverage returns uncovered conflicts.
Last-applied eligibility requires a nonempty decodable same-version typed object and removes fields added, removed or modified relative to live state.
Successful kubectl Apply updates an existing nonempty last-applied annotation; build/set failures return errors.
Last-applied updating requires a present nonempty annotation and encodes a copied apply object with that annotation removed.
StripMeta defines exact API identity and system metadata paths excluded from the current manager field set.
StripMeta subtracts only its listed paths and removes the manager if its remaining set is empty.
Capping considers Update entries only, sorts oldest first by timestamp then manager key, and bypasses lists at or below the cap.
Capping combines oldest Update field sets in versioned ancient-changes buckets and uses the more recent merged timestamp.
Update unions current-operation fields into the identified manager and changes its timestamp only when the operation owns changed fields.
Apply updates the manager timestamp when an object is returned; a no-change nil result copies live state without changing that timestamp.
ManagedFields validation accepts Apply/Update, rejects nonempty non-FieldsV1 type, validates manager and bounds subresource length.
Non-apply update uses live managed fields on subresources, accepts an explicit reset, otherwise decodes authored fields and falls back to live fields on invalid/empty decoded ownership.
Update removes request managed fields, updates ownership and re-encodes it; UpdateNoErrors logs failures and returns the object with managedFields cleared.
Reset means a nonnil empty list or a list with exactly one zero ManagedFieldsEntry; nil is not an explicit reset.
Apply decodes live managed fields, forwards force, converts merge conflicts to conflict errors and re-encodes ownership.
Managed-field decoding requires Apply/Update, nonempty apiVersion and FieldsV1, builds the manager key and decodes the field trie.
BuildManagerIdentifier clears fieldsType, fieldsV1 and time; for Apply it also clears apiVersion, then JSON-encodes the remaining manager, operation and subresource identity.
A nil fieldsV1 selects the empty field set; present raw FieldsV1 is converted with FieldsToSet.
FieldsToSet reads the raw bytes through fieldpath.Set.FromJSON; SetToFields uses Set.ToJSON.
FieldsV1.UnmarshalJSON retains the raw token without validating the trie; a null token does not replace raw bytes.
Apply checks the exact endpoint group/version, rejects nonnil metadata.managedFields, converts patch and live objects to typed values and calls the structured-merge updater with force.
Built-in and CRD structured-merge managers install the supplied strategy reset fields as the updater IgnoreFilter.
Create uses UpdateNoErrors with an empty live object and fieldManager or user-agent-derived manager.
Replacement update invokes UpdateNoErrors with live and new objects while managed-field updates are enabled; the disabled branch returns the new object.
After an object-size rejection before storage commit, the update handler clears submitted managedFields, disables their update and retries the request.
Apply patch decoding constructs an unstructured patch and invokes FieldManager.Apply with request manager and force.
ConfigMap storage supplies no resource-specific reset-fields strategy or status route.
REST installation constructs the field manager with available strategy reset fields and the selected subresource.
BeforeDelete validates DeleteOptions and UID/version preconditions, normalizes negative grace to one second and checks whether the strategy supports graceful deletion.
Graceful deletion can shorten an existing grace period, resumes a zero-grace interrupted delete, assigns deletion time and grace and increments positive generation on first graceful delete.
Orphan policy precedence is explicit DeleteOptions, existing orphan/foreground finalizers, then the strategy default; Unsupported bypasses orphan behavior.
Foreground policy is chosen from explicit DeleteOptions then existing foreground/orphan finalizers; absent selection is not foreground.
Garbage-collection finalizer adjustment is conditional on store GC support; it removes old GC tokens, applies selected tokens and retains other finalizers.
markAsDeleting sets zero grace, chooses the earlier deletion time and increments positive generation when deletion first begins.
Deletion updates run under storage preconditions and validation; a non-graceful object with finalizers is retained and marked deleting.
ShouldDeleteDuringUpdate requires no remaining finalizers, an old deletion timestamp and old grace that is absent or zero.
Store update turns the finalizer-empty deletion predicate into deletion through errEmptiedFinalizers.
Immediate delete invokes storage Delete with preconditions and reports storage errors before finalizing its response.
Namespace DELETE fills/checks UID and checks an explicit resource-version precondition.
First Namespace DELETE stores deletionTimestamp and Terminating under storage preconditions.
Namespace DELETE returns pending and later delegates only with no spec finalizers; delete-during-update also requires their absence.

crossFieldConditions: A reference does not grant access or prove an owner exists. GC identity includes the actual owner UID; reusing a name with a new UID leaves the old reference dangling.
A namespaced owner must be in the dependent namespace; a cluster-scoped dependent cannot use a namespaced owner. This reference has no namespace override.
Only one true controller reference is allowed. controller does not determine whether a reference is an ownership edge; other owners also prevent collection while solid.

With OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement enabled, changing references after creation requires delete permission on the dependent. New blockOwnerDeletion:true requires update permission on mapped owner finalizers, or the wildcard finalizers grant. Mapping/authorization failures reject admission; the comment mentioning owner delete permission is not the exact authorization record.

GC operates from an informer-built graph but rereads objects and checks UID before destructive actions. A solid owner retains a dependent; no solid owner permits GC. Foreground waits only for blocking dependents known to that graph.

Mapping/GET/patch/delete errors can postpone GC and be rate-limited for retry; invalid cluster-to-namespace ownership is forgotten by the delete worker rather than fixed by repeated retries. Check scope, coordinates and the fresh UID before repairing a reference.

Orphan deletion uses a snapshot of dependents known to the GC graph. The worker patches those dependents concurrently to remove the selected owner UID; its strategic patch includes the dependent UID as a precondition. NotFound is tolerated. Other failures can leave only some dependents changed and retain the owner orphan finalizer. The worker retries with rate limiting and removes that token only after dependent patching succeeds; a failed token update also retries. This sequence does not delete the dependent workloads or prove that every external resource is inventoried.
This dependent is cluster scoped. GC cannot resolve a namespaced owner for it.

managedFields records field ownership, not authentication or permission. The fieldManager request option (or user-agent fallback on non-apply requests), operation, endpoint version and subresource generate manager data; manually writing a manager name grants no access.

Non-apply root update distinguishes nil/omission from [] or [{}]: nil/empty decoded ownership falls back to the live object. Typed [] and a single zero entry select reset. With an existing live UID and empty ownership, the installed skip wrapper returns without tracking this update. Default create tracking probability is 1. A later Apply first records existing fields under before-first-apply. A subresource uses live ownership instead of request entries. CRD full-body coercion omits an empty [] before this selection; [{}] survives.

The metadata validator allows empty fieldsType, but DecodeManagedFields requires FieldsV1 and a nonempty apiVersion. A raw FieldsV1 token can decode without being a valid field trie. Update falls back to live ownership on decode failure; UpdateNoErrors clears ownership on later internal failure. Apply reports live-ownership decode errors and conflicts.

BuildManagerIdentifier excludes fieldsType, fieldsV1 and time. Update identity retains apiVersion; Apply identity removes apiVersion. manager, operation and subresource remain. The encoded versioned field set still retains its apiVersion.

The installed Apply version wrapper requires the full endpoint group/version/kind. Structured merge disallows nonnil authored managedFields. Request force is passed inward, but the exact manager kubectl has a last-applied migration exception: after conflicts, a nonempty valid same-version last-applied annotation permits an internal force=true retry only when all conflicting paths are covered and still equal their live values. Missing, malformed, wrong-version or unconvertible annotation leaves the original conflict. Partially covered conflicts return only the uncovered conflicts, without a forced retry. Resolve a conflict by inspecting the current fields and managers and changing ownership intent; force transfers conflicting ownership and can change another manager’s fields.

StripMeta removes apiVersion, kind, the metadata container path, and metadata name, namespace, creationTimestamp, selfLink, uid, clusterName, generation, managedFields and resourceVersion from the current manager field set; this is ownership exclusion, not removal from the stored object. Labels, annotations, finalizers and owners are not in this strip list. Update timestamps change when current-operation fields are recorded; an unchanged Apply preserves its prior manager time. Capping sorts Update entries by time then manager key and merges same-version entries into ancient-changes buckets. Apply entries are not capped. Distinct version buckets can prevent reducing the total to the configured cap of 10.

Successful exact kubectl Apply refreshes an existing nonempty kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation from a copied apply object without that annotation. Other managers and absent/empty annotations skip this update; encoding or setting failures return errors.

Strategy reset-field filters exclude fields that preparation restores; the status field-manager identity is distinct through subresource. Read the response after reset or conflict recovery. Do not assume a cleared managedFields list means apply succeeded or that all future conflicts disappear.

These are typed built-ins. Fresh null decodes managedFields to nil; [] remains a nonnil empty slice and [{}] remains one zero entry. Root non-apply field management selects reset for []/[{}], while omission/null falls back to live ownership. With a live UID and empty ownership, the installed skip wrapper skips tracking; reset does not immediately record the replacing manager. On create, the default wrapper tracks with probability 1. The supported status and finalize field-management route selects live ownership instead of request entries.

Deletion is a DELETE operation with DeleteOptions; writing timestamps or grace values in metadata is not a replacement for DELETE. Root create wipes those fields. Update preserves existing nonzero deletion time and fills absent old grace; immutable validation rejects an effective change that survives preparation.

Explicit propagation options override existing GC tokens and resource defaults. Foreground adds foregroundDeletion; orphan adds orphan; background removes those GC tokens. Other finalizers remain. GC unsupported/disabled branches do not install tokens that cannot be handled.

A DELETE response can mean deletion is pending. Pending finalizers retain the object with deletionTimestamp and zero grace for non-graceful resources. No new token may be added after stored deletion begins. Removing the last token can trigger delete during update when the old stored grace is absent or zero; this predicate does not compare a wall-clock deadline.

Retain finalizers until the responsible controller completes cleanup. Read fresh object UID, deletionTimestamp, finalizers and dependent state after timeout or partial failure. A missing object/new UID is a different lifetime; do not remove another lifetime’s finalizer. Check the external cleanup before manually removing a stuck token.

Orphan deletion uses a snapshot of dependents known to the GC graph. The worker patches those dependents concurrently to remove the selected owner UID; its strategic patch includes the dependent UID as a precondition. NotFound is tolerated. Other failures can leave only some dependents changed and retain the owner orphan finalizer. The worker retries with rate limiting and removes that token only after dependent patching succeeds; a failed token update also retries. This sequence does not delete the dependent workloads or prove that every external resource is inventoried.

ConfigMap, PVC and Service use ordinary non-graceful resource strategies: metadata grace does not select a Pod-like termination interval. Namespace has a separate DELETE implementation and two finalizer lists. Its first DELETE checks UID/version, stores Terminating and deletionTimestamp, and returns pending; later removal requires empty spec.finalizers as well as generic metadata-finalizer checks.

evidence.claim: Create requires a generated or explicit name and runs shared metadata checks.
Shared metadata validates scope, nonnegative generation, labels, annotations, ownership, finalizers and managed fields.
Owner-reference validation requires nonempty version/kind/name/UID, disallows v1 Event owners and permits at most one true controller pointer.
When OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement is enabled, changed references on non-create operations require delete permission on the dependent; unchanged and whitelisted requests bypass this check.
New blocking owner references require finalizers authorization; an update-finalizers wildcard grant bypasses REST mapping, otherwise every mapped owner is authorized.
Owner mapping requests update on the owner finalizers subresource; a namespaced owner uses the dependent namespace.
GC resolves the owner type and scope, rejects a namespaced owner of a cluster-dependent, fetches in the dependent namespace and treats NotFound or UID mismatch as dangling.
GC rereads the dependent, checks its UID, handles deleting owners and classifies the current owner references before deletion.
A solid owner prevents collection; dangling/waiting refs can be removed. Waiting-owner cycles can unblock references; no solid owner selects orphan, foreground or background deletion.
blockingDependents selects graph edges to this owner UID whose blockOwnerDeletion pointer is true.
Foreground GC retains the owner token while blocking dependents remain; otherwise it removes its foreground token.
Delete worker forgets stale virtual items and invalid cluster-to-namespace ownership, and returns retry for other errors including mapping failures.
The graph tracks current owner references and updates dependent edges when references are added, removed or changed.
Orphaning patches graph-known dependents concurrently, supplies dependent UID in the strategic patch and tolerates NotFound.
The orphan operation waits for all dependent attempts and returns aggregated non-NotFound failures.
The orphan worker forgets completed items and rate-limits retries for failed work.
The worker snapshots graph dependents and removes the owner orphan finalizer only after dependent patching succeeds; finalizer update failure also retries.
The default Update-manager cap is 10 and default create tracking probability is 1.
NewDefaultFieldManager installs version checking, last-applied updating/migration, skip-non-applied, manager capping, manager identity, time updating and metadata stripping wrappers.
Empty ownership on an existing live UID skips non-apply tracking; create tracking uses the configured probability.
Apply with empty ownership first records live fields under before-first-apply and returns bootstrap errors.
Apply rejects a full group/version/kind different from the configured endpoint.
Only exact kubectl handles merge conflicts through last-applied eligibility; complete coverage retries with force true and partial coverage returns uncovered conflicts.
Last-applied eligibility requires a nonempty decodable same-version typed object and removes fields added, removed or modified relative to live state.
Successful kubectl Apply updates an existing nonempty last-applied annotation; build/set failures return errors.
Last-applied updating requires a present nonempty annotation and encodes a copied apply object with that annotation removed.
StripMeta defines exact API identity and system metadata paths excluded from the current manager field set.
StripMeta subtracts only its listed paths and removes the manager if its remaining set is empty.
Capping considers Update entries only, sorts oldest first by timestamp then manager key, and bypasses lists at or below the cap.
Capping combines oldest Update field sets in versioned ancient-changes buckets and uses the more recent merged timestamp.
Update unions current-operation fields into the identified manager and changes its timestamp only when the operation owns changed fields.
Apply updates the manager timestamp when an object is returned; a no-change nil result copies live state without changing that timestamp.
ManagedFields validation accepts Apply/Update, rejects nonempty non-FieldsV1 type, validates manager and bounds subresource length.
Non-apply update uses live managed fields on subresources, accepts an explicit reset, otherwise decodes authored fields and falls back to live fields on invalid/empty decoded ownership.
Update removes request managed fields, updates ownership and re-encodes it; UpdateNoErrors logs failures and returns the object with managedFields cleared.
Reset means a nonnil empty list or a list with exactly one zero ManagedFieldsEntry; nil is not an explicit reset.
Apply decodes live managed fields, forwards force, converts merge conflicts to conflict errors and re-encodes ownership.
Managed-field decoding requires Apply/Update, nonempty apiVersion and FieldsV1, builds the manager key and decodes the field trie.
BuildManagerIdentifier clears fieldsType, fieldsV1 and time; for Apply it also clears apiVersion, then JSON-encodes the remaining manager, operation and subresource identity.
A nil fieldsV1 selects the empty field set; present raw FieldsV1 is converted with FieldsToSet.
FieldsToSet reads the raw bytes through fieldpath.Set.FromJSON; SetToFields uses Set.ToJSON.
FieldsV1.UnmarshalJSON retains the raw token without validating the trie; a null token does not replace raw bytes.
Apply checks the exact endpoint group/version, rejects nonnil metadata.managedFields, converts patch and live objects to typed values and calls the structured-merge updater with force.
Built-in and CRD structured-merge managers install the supplied strategy reset fields as the updater IgnoreFilter.
Create uses UpdateNoErrors with an empty live object and fieldManager or user-agent-derived manager.
Replacement update invokes UpdateNoErrors with live and new objects while managed-field updates are enabled; the disabled branch returns the new object.
After an object-size rejection before storage commit, the update handler clears submitted managedFields, disables their update and retries the request.
Apply patch decoding constructs an unstructured patch and invokes FieldManager.Apply with request manager and force.
The concrete root strategy exposes its field-manager reset-field set.
REST installation constructs the field manager with available strategy reset fields and the selected subresource.
BeforeDelete validates DeleteOptions and UID/version preconditions, normalizes negative grace to one second and checks whether the strategy supports graceful deletion.
Graceful deletion can shorten an existing grace period, resumes a zero-grace interrupted delete, assigns deletion time and grace and increments positive generation on first graceful delete.
Orphan policy precedence is explicit DeleteOptions, existing orphan/foreground finalizers, then the strategy default; Unsupported bypasses orphan behavior.
Foreground policy is chosen from explicit DeleteOptions then existing foreground/orphan finalizers; absent selection is not foreground.
Garbage-collection finalizer adjustment is conditional on store GC support; it removes old GC tokens, applies selected tokens and retains other finalizers.
markAsDeleting sets zero grace, chooses the earlier deletion time and increments positive generation when deletion first begins.
Deletion updates run under storage preconditions and validation; a non-graceful object with finalizers is retained and marked deleting.
ShouldDeleteDuringUpdate requires no remaining finalizers, an old deletion timestamp and old grace that is absent or zero.
Store update turns the finalizer-empty deletion predicate into deletion through errEmptiedFinalizers.
Immediate delete invokes storage Delete with preconditions and reports storage errors before finalizing its response.
Namespace DELETE fills/checks UID and checks an explicit resource-version precondition.
First Namespace DELETE stores deletionTimestamp and Terminating under storage preconditions.
Namespace DELETE returns pending and later delegates only with no spec finalizers; delete-during-update also requires their absence.

These normal resource strategies allow unconditional update: absent resourceVersion can be filled from storage rather than establish a compare-and-swap precondition. Supply the observed resourceVersion to protect a conditional update.

KubeClaw configuration/workspace claims and Prism database/artifact claims default their chart storageClass values to empty. Their templates omit storageClassName for that value, so admission or binding can select a cluster default. An explicitly empty API storageClassName instead requests no class. The registered SMB chart 1.20.0 is a candidate driver, not proof that these claims select it; inspect the stored claim, StorageClass provisioner, PV CSI driver and controller images.

For an omitted claim class, the default-class helper recognizes the exact string true in either stable or beta default annotation. It selects the newest creation timestamp among defaults, breaking equal timestamp ties by ascending class name. No default yields no class; listing or PVC-update errors stop that attempt. The binder can later assign a discovered default to an unclassified claim. Observe the actual stored class and its provisioner rather than selecting SMB from installation alone.

The KubeClaw configuration/workspace PVCs and Prism artifacts/backups PVCs carry Helm keep and Argo Prune=false,Delete=false annotations. Prism database claim-template metadata carries Argo Prune=false,Delete=false. These persistence controls mean ordinary release removal is not the operator-retirement deletion route described here; inspect the rendered object, owner/workload policy and GitOps operation before any explicit retirement.

After a bound claim disappears, the PV controller checks its claim reference and UID, including fallback reads when needed, before recording Released. A different live UID is another claim lifetime. A lookup or phase-write error stops that sync; an existing Failed phase is preserved. PV Retain performs no reclaim operation. Delete dispatches deletion, but an external CSI deleter is left to its provisioner. PVC protection removal alone performs none of these steps.

The selected external-provisioner library reconciles only PVs owned by its provisioner or CSI driver. Its deletion guard requires Released and Delete, with deletionTimestamp/finalizer checks determined by its configured addFinalizer option. It calls the CSI provisioner Delete first, then requests PV deletion and removes its own finalizer when configured. IgnoredError leaves the work to another owner; another error emits VolumeFailedDelete. A PV-delete or finalizer-patch failure after a successful driver call leaves partial progress and can repeat the driver call.

The CSI provisioner Delete uses the PV CSI volume handle, checks driver capabilities, resolves deletion credentials and checks VolumeAttachments when its lister exists. A matching attachment or list error blocks the RPC; no lister adds no attachment check. Missing or unreadable deletion credentials can still allow DeleteVolume with no secrets on the documented branches. The RPC uses the provisioner timeout. Queue retry continues while the configured failed-delete threshold allows it; zero has no threshold stop, and reaching a nonzero threshold stops rate-limited requeue without forgetting the counter. Do not assume an unlimited retry or successful external deletion from an API observation.

SMB v1.20.0 DeleteVolume rejects an empty handle, treats an unparseable handle as already absent, and uses an in-process per-volume lock. With no secrets, or with effective onDelete Retain, it returns success without deleting the subdirectory. With secrets and a non-Retain policy, it mounts the base share, then Archive renames the subdirectory to archived-<subdirectory>; when removeArchivedVolumePath is enabled, it first removes an earlier archive. Other non-Retain policies remove the subdirectory. Mount, archive or removal errors propagate; deferred unmount failure is only logged. Even a no-directory-work success stores the handle in the in-process deletion cache. A later call with secrets can return cached success without new directory work; this is not durable data-recovery evidence.

Before any retry or cleanup change, the storage owner must retain claim/PV UID, volume handle, reclaim policy, effective SMB onDelete/default policy, driver options, non-secret credential-reference identity, events and logs. Check the actual share and archived path through the approved storage process. Do not remove finalizers or delete a retained directory to force convergence. A completed RemoveAll or removal of an earlier archive has no rollback in this implementation. Archive on the same share and a successful DeleteVolume response are not independent backups or application recovery; follow the separately verified recovery procedure or stop before cutover.

crossFieldConditions: A reference does not grant access or prove an owner exists. GC identity includes the actual owner UID; reusing a name with a new UID leaves the old reference dangling.
A namespaced owner must be in the dependent namespace; a cluster-scoped dependent cannot use a namespaced owner. This reference has no namespace override.
Only one true controller reference is allowed. controller does not determine whether a reference is an ownership edge; other owners also prevent collection while solid.

With OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement enabled, changing references after creation requires delete permission on the dependent. New blockOwnerDeletion:true requires update permission on mapped owner finalizers, or the wildcard finalizers grant. Mapping/authorization failures reject admission; the comment mentioning owner delete permission is not the exact authorization record.

GC operates from an informer-built graph but rereads objects and checks UID before destructive actions. A solid owner retains a dependent; no solid owner permits GC. Foreground waits only for blocking dependents known to that graph.

Mapping/GET/patch/delete errors can postpone GC and be rate-limited for retry; invalid cluster-to-namespace ownership is forgotten by the delete worker rather than fixed by repeated retries. Check scope, coordinates and the fresh UID before repairing a reference.

Orphan deletion uses a snapshot of dependents known to the GC graph. The worker patches those dependents concurrently to remove the selected owner UID; its strategic patch includes the dependent UID as a precondition. NotFound is tolerated. Other failures can leave only some dependents changed and retain the owner orphan finalizer. The worker retries with rate limiting and removes that token only after dependent patching succeeds; a failed token update also retries. This sequence does not delete the dependent workloads or prove that every external resource is inventoried.
This dependent is namespaced. A namespaced owner is looked up in this dependent namespace; cluster-scoped owners are resolved without a namespace.

managedFields records field ownership, not authentication or permission. The fieldManager request option (or user-agent fallback on non-apply requests), operation, endpoint version and subresource generate manager data; manually writing a manager name grants no access.

Non-apply root update distinguishes nil/omission from [] or [{}]: nil/empty decoded ownership falls back to the live object. Typed [] and a single zero entry select reset. With an existing live UID and empty ownership, the installed skip wrapper returns without tracking this update. Default create tracking probability is 1. A later Apply first records existing fields under before-first-apply. A subresource uses live ownership instead of request entries. CRD full-body coercion omits an empty [] before this selection; [{}] survives.

The metadata validator allows empty fieldsType, but DecodeManagedFields requires FieldsV1 and a nonempty apiVersion. A raw FieldsV1 token can decode without being a valid field trie. Update falls back to live ownership on decode failure; UpdateNoErrors clears ownership on later internal failure. Apply reports live-ownership decode errors and conflicts.

BuildManagerIdentifier excludes fieldsType, fieldsV1 and time. Update identity retains apiVersion; Apply identity removes apiVersion. manager, operation and subresource remain. The encoded versioned field set still retains its apiVersion.

The installed Apply version wrapper requires the full endpoint group/version/kind. Structured merge disallows nonnil authored managedFields. Request force is passed inward, but the exact manager kubectl has a last-applied migration exception: after conflicts, a nonempty valid same-version last-applied annotation permits an internal force=true retry only when all conflicting paths are covered and still equal their live values. Missing, malformed, wrong-version or unconvertible annotation leaves the original conflict. Partially covered conflicts return only the uncovered conflicts, without a forced retry. Resolve a conflict by inspecting the current fields and managers and changing ownership intent; force transfers conflicting ownership and can change another manager’s fields.

StripMeta removes apiVersion, kind, the metadata container path, and metadata name, namespace, creationTimestamp, selfLink, uid, clusterName, generation, managedFields and resourceVersion from the current manager field set; this is ownership exclusion, not removal from the stored object. Labels, annotations, finalizers and owners are not in this strip list. Update timestamps change when current-operation fields are recorded; an unchanged Apply preserves its prior manager time. Capping sorts Update entries by time then manager key and merges same-version entries into ancient-changes buckets. Apply entries are not capped. Distinct version buckets can prevent reducing the total to the configured cap of 10.

Successful exact kubectl Apply refreshes an existing nonempty kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation from a copied apply object without that annotation. Other managers and absent/empty annotations skip this update; encoding or setting failures return errors.

Strategy reset-field filters exclude fields that preparation restores; the status field-manager identity is distinct through subresource. Read the response after reset or conflict recovery. Do not assume a cleared managedFields list means apply succeeded or that all future conflicts disappear.

These are typed built-ins. Fresh null decodes managedFields to nil; [] remains a nonnil empty slice and [{}] remains one zero entry. Root non-apply field management selects reset for []/[{}], while omission/null falls back to live ownership. With a live UID and empty ownership, the installed skip wrapper skips tracking; reset does not immediately record the replacing manager. On create, the default wrapper tracks with probability 1. The supported status field-management route selects live ownership instead of request entries.

Deletion is a DELETE operation with DeleteOptions; writing timestamps or grace values in metadata is not a replacement for DELETE. Root create wipes those fields. Update preserves existing nonzero deletion time and fills absent old grace; immutable validation rejects an effective change that survives preparation.

Explicit propagation options override existing GC tokens and resource defaults. Foreground adds foregroundDeletion; orphan adds orphan; background removes those GC tokens. Other finalizers remain. GC unsupported/disabled branches do not install tokens that cannot be handled.

A DELETE response can mean deletion is pending. Pending finalizers retain the object with deletionTimestamp and zero grace for non-graceful resources. No new token may be added after stored deletion begins. Removing the last token can trigger delete during update when the old stored grace is absent or zero; this predicate does not compare a wall-clock deadline.

Retain finalizers until the responsible controller completes cleanup. Read fresh object UID, deletionTimestamp, finalizers and dependent state after timeout or partial failure. A missing object/new UID is a different lifetime; do not remove another lifetime’s finalizer. Check the external cleanup before manually removing a stuck token.

Orphan deletion uses a snapshot of dependents known to the GC graph. The worker patches those dependents concurrently to remove the selected owner UID; its strategic patch includes the dependent UID as a precondition. NotFound is tolerated. Other failures can leave only some dependents changed and retain the owner orphan finalizer. The worker retries with rate limiting and removes that token only after dependent patching succeeds; a failed token update also retries. This sequence does not delete the dependent workloads or prove that every external resource is inventoried.

ConfigMap, PVC and Service use ordinary non-graceful resource strategies: metadata grace does not select a Pod-like termination interval. Namespace has a separate DELETE implementation and two finalizer lists. Its first DELETE checks UID/version, stores Terminating and deletionTimestamp, and returns pending; later removal requires empty spec.finalizers as well as generic metadata-finalizer checks.

Owner mapping requests update on the owner finalizers subresource; a namespaced owner uses the dependent namespace.
GC resolves the owner type and scope, rejects a namespaced owner of a cluster-dependent, fetches in the dependent namespace and treats NotFound or UID mismatch as dangling.
GC rereads the dependent, checks its UID, handles deleting owners and classifies the current owner references before deletion.
A solid owner prevents collection; dangling/waiting refs can be removed. Waiting-owner cycles can unblock references; no solid owner selects orphan, foreground or background deletion.
blockingDependents selects graph edges to this owner UID whose blockOwnerDeletion pointer is true.
Foreground GC retains the owner token while blocking dependents remain; otherwise it removes its foreground token.
Delete worker forgets stale virtual items and invalid cluster-to-namespace ownership, and returns retry for other errors including mapping failures.
The graph tracks current owner references and updates dependent edges when references are added, removed or changed.
Orphaning patches graph-known dependents concurrently, supplies dependent UID in the strategic patch and tolerates NotFound.
The orphan operation waits for all dependent attempts and returns aggregated non-NotFound failures.
The orphan worker forgets completed items and rate-limits retries for failed work.
The worker snapshots graph dependents and removes the owner orphan finalizer only after dependent patching succeeds; finalizer update failure also retries.
The default Update-manager cap is 10 and default create tracking probability is 1.
NewDefaultFieldManager installs version checking, last-applied updating/migration, skip-non-applied, manager capping, manager identity, time updating and metadata stripping wrappers.
Empty ownership on an existing live UID skips non-apply tracking; create tracking uses the configured probability.
Apply with empty ownership first records live fields under before-first-apply and returns bootstrap errors.
Apply rejects a full group/version/kind different from the configured endpoint.
Only exact kubectl handles merge conflicts through last-applied eligibility; complete coverage retries with force true and partial coverage returns uncovered conflicts.

Successful kubectl Apply updates an existing nonempty last-applied annotation; build/set failures return errors.
Last-applied updating requires a present nonempty annotation and encodes a copied apply object with that annotation removed.
StripMeta defines exact API identity and system metadata paths excluded from the current manager field set.
StripMeta subtracts only its listed paths and removes the manager if its remaining set is empty.
Capping considers Update entries only, sorts oldest first by timestamp then manager key, and bypasses lists at or below the cap.
Capping combines oldest Update field sets in versioned ancient-changes buckets and uses the more recent merged timestamp.
Update unions current-operation fields into the identified manager and changes its timestamp only when the operation owns changed fields.
Apply updates the manager timestamp when an object is returned; a no-change nil result copies live state without changing that timestamp.
ManagedFields validation accepts Apply/Update, rejects nonempty non-FieldsV1 type, validates manager and bounds subresource length.
Non-apply update uses live managed fields on subresources, accepts an explicit reset, otherwise decodes authored fields and falls back to live fields on invalid/empty decoded ownership.
Update removes request managed fields, updates ownership and re-encodes it; UpdateNoErrors logs failures and returns the object with managedFields cleared.
Reset means a nonnil empty list or a list with exactly one zero ManagedFieldsEntry; nil is not an explicit reset.
Apply decodes live managed fields, forwards force, converts merge conflicts to conflict errors and re-encodes ownership.
Managed-field decoding requires Apply/Update, nonempty apiVersion and FieldsV1, builds the manager key and decodes the field trie.
BuildManagerIdentifier clears fieldsType, fieldsV1 and time; for Apply it also clears apiVersion, then JSON-encodes the remaining manager, operation and subresource identity.
A nil fieldsV1 selects the empty field set; present raw FieldsV1 is converted with FieldsToSet.
FieldsToSet reads the raw bytes through fieldpath.Set.FromJSON; SetToFields uses Set.ToJSON.
FieldsV1.UnmarshalJSON retains the raw token without validating the trie; a null token does not replace raw bytes.
Apply checks the exact endpoint group/version, rejects nonnil metadata.managedFields, converts patch and live objects to typed values and calls the structured-merge updater with force.
Built-in and CRD structured-merge managers install the supplied strategy reset fields as the updater IgnoreFilter.
Create uses UpdateNoErrors with an empty live object and fieldManager or user-agent-derived manager.
Replacement update invokes UpdateNoErrors with live and new objects while managed-field updates are enabled; the disabled branch returns the new object.
After an object-size rejection before storage commit, the update handler clears submitted managedFields, disables their update and retries the request.
Apply patch decoding constructs an unstructured patch and invokes FieldManager.Apply with request manager and force.
The concrete root strategy exposes its field-manager reset-field set.
REST installation constructs the field manager with available strategy reset fields and the selected subresource.
BeforeDelete validates DeleteOptions and UID/version preconditions, normalizes negative grace to one second and checks whether the strategy supports graceful deletion.
Graceful deletion can shorten an existing grace period, resumes a zero-grace interrupted delete, assigns deletion time and grace and increments positive generation on first graceful delete.
Orphan policy precedence is explicit DeleteOptions, existing orphan/foreground finalizers, then the strategy default; Unsupported bypasses orphan behavior.
Foreground policy is chosen from explicit DeleteOptions then existing foreground/orphan finalizers; absent selection is not foreground.
Garbage-collection finalizer adjustment is conditional on store GC support; it removes old GC tokens, applies selected tokens and retains other finalizers.
markAsDeleting sets zero grace, chooses the earlier deletion time and increments positive generation when deletion first begins.
Deletion updates run under storage preconditions and validation; a non-graceful object with finalizers is retained and marked deleting.
ShouldDeleteDuringUpdate requires no remaining finalizers, an old deletion timestamp and old grace that is absent or zero.
Store update turns the finalizer-empty deletion predicate into deletion through errEmptiedFinalizers.
Immediate delete invokes storage Delete with preconditions and reports storage errors before finalizing its response.
Namespace DELETE fills/checks UID and checks an explicit resource-version precondition.
First Namespace DELETE stores deletionTimestamp and Terminating under storage preconditions.
Namespace DELETE returns pending and later delegates only with no spec finalizers; delete-during-update also requires their absence.

The ordinary endpoint preserves stored status; bound status determines the allowed request-size and volume-attributes exceptions.

PVC spec is immutable except the exact update branches for one-time volumeName, storage-class upgrades, bound storage requests and volume attributes. A change permitted by API validation is not proof that storage expansion or data population succeeds.

For an unbound claim with empty volumeName, the pinned PV controller searches a matching PV. If none exists, it can assign a default class, wait for delayed binding, start provisioning for a nonempty class, or record FailedBinding and retain Pending. A nonempty volumeName selects the separate named-PV branch. Binding writes PV identity/status before PVC volumeName/annotations and Bound status; it stops on the first write error, so a partial result must be read before retry.

FindMatchingVolume compares effective claim/PV volumeAttributesClassName values after nil becomes empty. With volume-attributes matching enabled it skips unequal classes. With matching disabled it skips any PV with a nonempty class; a valid claim name alone does not establish a matching PV.

Kubelet resolves the claim in the Pod namespace and requires Bound phase and a nonempty volumeName. It retrieves that PV and requires a nonnil claimRef with the exact claim UID. Passing these checks creates the PV volume spec; it does not prove attach/mount or successful filesystem access.

The PV controller selects its previously-bound reconciliation by the bind-completed annotation, not by phase alone. For an unbound claim with explicit volumeName it looks up that named PV rather than falling back to a newly provisioned volume. A missing named PV records Pending. For an unclaimed named PV, deletion state, capacity, storage class, feature-selected attributes class, volume mode and access modes must satisfy the claim; failure emits VolumeMismatch and records Pending. A matching pre-bound claim reference instead completes bind; the helper matches name/namespace and any nonempty reference UID.

If the named PV belongs to another claim, the explicit-selection branch emits FailedBinding. Without the bound-by-controller annotation it records Pending and waits for later sync. With that annotation it returns an invalid-binding error. Lookup, bind and status-write errors propagate, so read both objects after partial progress rather than changing a PV claim reference to force success.

For a claim with bind-completed recorded, an empty volumeName or missing cached PV records Lost with ClaimLost. A PV claimRef UID different from the PVC UID records Lost with ClaimMisbound. Those no-volume status updates clear observed accessModes, capacity and current attributes class when present. Lost is a controller observation of missing or conflicting binding, not an independently checked erasure of server data.

A previously-bound claim whose PV claimRef is nil can be rebound by the controller; a matching claimRef UID also calls bind to finish or repair observations. The controller cannot distinguish a genuinely unbound PV from an older cache view in the nil-reference branch. A bind or API write error can leave partial PV/PVC state. Preserve original UIDs/handle, inspect live references and events, and involve the storage owner before any replacement or recovery; this branch does not migrate or restore data.

The conditional SMB chart 1.20.0 route below uses its default driver v1.20.0, external-provisioner v6.0.0 and external-resizer v2.0.0. It does not infer that every PVC selects SMB or that these images are deployed. Read the claim class, StorageClass provisioner, PV driver and actual image versions before using this route.

The selected external-provisioner prefers dataSource over dataSourceRef. When dataSource is absent and the CrossNamespaceVolumeDataSource gate is off, it rejects a nonempty dataSourceRef.namespace; nil or empty namespace does not trigger that rejection. A local source uses the claim namespace. For another namespace it lists ReferenceGrants there. A grant must permit a core PersistentVolumeClaim from the claim namespace and the target group/kind plus absent, empty or matching target name. Failure stops source resolution; API admission alone does not authorize source access.

This provisioner handles PVC clones and snapshot.storage.k8s.io VolumeSnapshot sources. Another kind produces an IgnoredError and an event saying an external populator is expected; it does not create a populated volume itself. A nonnil claim selector is rejected for dynamic CSI provisioning, even if the core binding controller can match an existing PV with that selector.

When its VolumeAttributesClass feature is enabled, this provisioner requires MODIFY_VOLUME for a nonempty volumeAttributesClassName before CreateVolume. SMB v1.20.0 advertises CREATE_DELETE_VOLUME, SINGLE_NODE_MULTI_WRITER, CLONE_VOLUME and EXPAND_VOLUME, but not MODIFY_VOLUME. On that selected route, the capability check rejects this claim; API acceptance of the name does not establish provisioning or volume modification support.

A clone source must be Bound, not deleting, have class and volume identity, and fit the requested size. Its PV must use the destination class provisioner, have the exact source claim UID/namespace/name, be Bound and have the same Block/Filesystem mode. A snapshot source must not be deleting, must have bound content with matching UID/namespace/name and driver, ReadyToUse true and a snapshot handle. Requested capacity must cover restoreSize when present; enabled mode-conversion protection checks the snapshot-content permission annotation.

SMB v1.20.0 rejects Block capability. Its snapshot RPCs are Unimplemented and its content-copy route rejects a snapshot source; a valid PVC snapshot reference cannot establish snapshot restore on SMB. Its PVC-clone route copies from the source SMB volume. Copy, SMB access and application consistency are separate from core binding.

On the selected SMB clone route, copyFromVolume parses the source handle, uses the first requested capability when present, and mounts source and destination through NodeStageVolume with the same CreateVolume secrets. An invalid source handle returns NotFound; either mount can fail. It then runs external cp -a from the source directory contents to the destination. Copy failure returns Internal with command output and does not undo a partially written destination. The command is not bound to RPC context cancellation, and deferred unmount errors only log warnings. Preserve both handles and inspect destination contents/mounts after a timeout or error; do not replay or delete the destination as if no copy occurred. This route does not quiesce the source application or verify an independently restored reader.

KubeClaw configuration/workspace claims and Prism database/artifact claims default their chart storageClass values to empty. Their templates omit storageClassName for that value, so admission or binding can select a cluster default. An explicitly empty API storageClassName instead requests no class. The registered SMB chart 1.20.0 is a candidate driver, not proof that these claims select it; inspect the stored claim, StorageClass provisioner, PV CSI driver and controller images.

For an omitted claim class, the default-class helper recognizes the exact string true in either stable or beta default annotation. It selects the newest creation timestamp among defaults, breaking equal timestamp ties by ascending class name. No default yields no class; listing or PVC-update errors stop that attempt. The binder can later assign a discovered default to an unclassified claim. Observe the actual stored class and its provisioner rather than selecting SMB from installation alone.

The KubeClaw configuration/workspace PVCs and Prism artifacts/backups PVCs carry Helm keep and Argo Prune=false,Delete=false annotations. Prism database claim-template metadata carries Argo Prune=false,Delete=false. These persistence controls mean ordinary release removal is not the operator-retirement deletion route described here; inspect the rendered object, owner/workload policy and GitOps operation before any explicit retirement.

After a bound claim disappears, the PV controller checks its claim reference and UID, including fallback reads when needed, before recording Released. A different live UID is another claim lifetime. A lookup or phase-write error stops that sync; an existing Failed phase is preserved. PV Retain performs no reclaim operation. Delete dispatches deletion, but an external CSI deleter is left to its provisioner. PVC protection removal alone performs none of these steps.

The selected external-provisioner library reconciles only PVs owned by its provisioner or CSI driver. Its deletion guard requires Released and Delete, with deletionTimestamp/finalizer checks determined by its configured addFinalizer option. It calls the CSI provisioner Delete first, then requests PV deletion and removes its own finalizer when configured. IgnoredError leaves the work to another owner; another error emits VolumeFailedDelete. A PV-delete or finalizer-patch failure after a successful driver call leaves partial progress and can repeat the driver call.

The CSI provisioner Delete uses the PV CSI volume handle, checks driver capabilities, resolves deletion credentials and checks VolumeAttachments when its lister exists. A matching attachment or list error blocks the RPC; no lister adds no attachment check. Missing or unreadable deletion credentials can still allow DeleteVolume with no secrets on the documented branches. The RPC uses the provisioner timeout. Queue retry continues while the configured failed-delete threshold allows it; zero has no threshold stop, and reaching a nonzero threshold stops rate-limited requeue without forgetting the counter. Do not assume an unlimited retry or successful external deletion from an API observation.

SMB v1.20.0 DeleteVolume rejects an empty handle, treats an unparseable handle as already absent, and uses an in-process per-volume lock. With no secrets, or with effective onDelete Retain, it returns success without deleting the subdirectory. With secrets and a non-Retain policy, it mounts the base share, then Archive renames the subdirectory to archived-<subdirectory>; when removeArchivedVolumePath is enabled, it first removes an earlier archive. Other non-Retain policies remove the subdirectory. Mount, archive or removal errors propagate; deferred unmount failure is only logged. Even a no-directory-work success stores the handle in the in-process deletion cache. A later call with secrets can return cached success without new directory work; this is not durable data-recovery evidence.

Before any retry or cleanup change, the storage owner must retain claim/PV UID, volume handle, reclaim policy, effective SMB onDelete/default policy, driver options, non-secret credential-reference identity, events and logs. Check the actual share and archived path through the approved storage process. Do not remove finalizers or delete a retained directory to force convergence. A completed RemoveAll or removal of an earlier archive has no rollback in this implementation. Archive on the same share and a successful DeleteVolume response are not independent backups or application recovery; follow the separately verified recovery procedure or stop before cutover.

After Bound/PV UID checks, CSI attach/mount is another receiving route. CSIDriver attachRequired:false skips attach; otherwise the controller creates/observes VolumeAttachment and Kubelet checks attachment. NodeStage runs only if the driver advertises STAGE_UNSTAGE_VOLUME; NodePublish receives read-only intent, mode, mount options and secrets. An RPC error can be uncertain, and an error after successful publication can leave the volume mounted.

SMB v1.20.0 NodeStage requires handle, capability, staging target and a source in volume context. It reads source/subDir and claim/PV metadata substitutions, uses a lock keyed by handle plus staging target, and resolves credentials from case-insensitive secret keys with trimmed username/password/domain. Guest mount options bypass username/password options. Persistent staging uses the supplied node-stage secrets; the separately identified ephemeral branch can fetch its configured Secret. Linux can use a Kerberos cache, create the staging directory and add the requested mount group when no gid flag is present; Windows uses its domain/username option path. Credential/cache/directory errors can stop before mounting and can leave local preparation artifacts.

SMB checks the actual staging mount point before work. An already-mounted readable target skips a new SMB mount. An unreadable existing target can be unmounted and still return its read error; inspect the actual target before retry. For a new mount it substitutes subDir metadata and calls Mount with the source, options and sensitive credentials through a 110-second WaitUntilTimeout wrapper. That wrapper returns the mount error or timeout without cancelling its mount goroutine. Inference from that wrapper and the deferred staging-lock release: timeout can leave mount work running after this call releases its lock. A failed staging response is not proof that the share is unmounted; retain handle/target and investigate current mounts and driver work before repeating it.

For SMB v1.20.0, persistent NodePublish binds the staging path to the container target, adding ro when requested. It can return success for an already-mounted target. Access to the actual SMB share, credentials, server data and application read/write checks remain necessary; Bound or successful mount is not a backup/restore proof.

SMB chart 1.20.0 defaults to driver v1.20.0, provisioner v6.0.0 and resizer v2.0.0. Image overrides select another receiving authority.
The provisioner resolves source precedence/namespace and checks cross-namespace grants.
IsGranted matches the source-namespace grant, core claim From identity and target group/kind/optional name; otherwise it returns an access error.
Provisioning selects clone/snapshot capability, leaves other kinds to a populator and rejects a nonnil selector.
An enabled nonempty volumeAttributesClassName sets the modifyVolume requirement before capability checking.
A modifyVolume requirement rejects a driver without MODIFY_VOLUME before CreateVolume.
The SMB driver capability list does not advertise MODIFY_VOLUME.
Clone source lookup requires Bound/non-deleting state, source/destination classes and sufficient destination requested size.
Clone PV lookup checks CSI driver, exact claim identity, Bound state and matching volume mode.
Snapshot resolution checks non-deleting/bound snapshot, exact content reference identity, driver and readiness.
Snapshot restore requires a handle, adequate restore size and permitted mode conversion when that protection is enabled.
SMB snapshot RPCs return Unimplemented.
SMB content copy rejects snapshot sources and dispatches volume clones to copyFromVolume.
SMB clone parsing establishes source/destination paths and selects the first supplied capability.
Source and destination use the same CreateVolume secrets for internal staging; mount failures return errors and deferred unmount failures only log.
SMB clone runs external cp -a without a context-bound command and returns copy errors without destination rollback.
Internal SMB mounts call NodeStageVolume with the base-share source, volume handle, staging path, capability and request secrets.
SMB capability validation rejects Block volumes.
Configuration/workspace storageClass defaults are empty.
Configuration PVC renders storageClassName only for a nonempty chart value.
Workspace PVC renders storageClassName only for a nonempty chart value.
Prism database/artifact storageClass defaults are empty.
Prism database claim template omits the class when its chart value is empty.
Prism artifact claim omits the class when its chart value is empty.
The registered SMB Application selects chart 1.20.0, not a class for every claim.

Default-class listing selects newest creation time and ascending name for timestamp ties; no defaults returns nil.
Stable or beta default annotation is recognized only when its value is exactly true.
Later class assignment skips classified claims, returns lookup/update errors and assigns an available default to an unclassified claim.
DefaultStorageClass skips a specified class, including an explicit empty pointer, and otherwise selects a default if available.
A missing cached bound claim is checked through lister and API reads before release; non-NotFound errors stop sync.
UID checks distinguish claim lifetimes; a missing bound claim records Released before reclaim while preserving Failed.
Reclaim dispatches Retain, Recycle and Delete; migrated PVs are left to the external provisioner.
A missing in-tree deleter leaves external deletion to its owner.
PV sync selects the responsible provisioner/driver before deletion reconciliation.
Deletion requires Released/Delete and respects the configured finalizer and deletion guard.
Driver Delete precedes PV deletion and optional finalizer removal; errors and IgnoredError have separate outcomes.
Failed deletion requeue obeys its configured threshold; success forgets the queue counter.
CSI Delete resolves the handle and capabilities, obtains secrets, bounds the RPC and checks attachments.
Recorded deletion-secret references can yield an empty secret map after a failed fetch; both empty references request no secret.
StorageClass fallback can continue without secrets when claim reference, class or credentials are unavailable.
A configured VolumeAttachment lister blocks deletion for list errors or matching attachments; nil skips that check.
SMB deletion validates or treats the handle as absent and locks the volume operation.
No secrets or Retain bypasses directory work; other policies use a deletion cache and mount the share.
Archive optionally removes an earlier archive, then renames the source directory; failures propagate.
Other policies remove the subdirectory; no-action and completion paths return success and cache the handle.
CSI attach can be skipped only through a CSIDriver attachRequired:false result; missing driver or lookup failure follows its explicit path.
Attach creates the VolumeAttachment and waits for its observed attachment result.
Node staging is conditional on capability and returns RPC errors with finished-operation cleanup.
NodePublish receives the resolved volume inputs; RPC errors propagate and a post-publication SELinux check can return uncertain progress.
SMB staging validates identity/capability/target and reads context, mount flags, group and secrets.
SMB resolves source/subdirectory metadata and holds a handle-plus-target lock.
SMB trims credential values, recognizes guest mounts and fetches a Secret only for its ephemeral branch.
Platform-specific staging sets Windows credentials or Linux Kerberos/directory/group/domain options.
Readable existing staging can skip mounting; a new mount substitutes subDir metadata and returns mount/timeout errors.
The SMB mount wait is configured for 110 seconds.
WaitUntilTimeout returns on its timer or goroutine result; it does not cancel the in-progress mount function.
An existing readable mount is accepted; a failed directory read can unmount the target and still return that read error.
Kerberos staging can write/chown a cache before a later symlink operation fails.
Persistent SMB NodePublish binds the staging path with optional ro, handles an already mounted target and reports mount/cleanup errors.

A snapshot source must not be deleting, must have bound content with matching UID/namespace/name and driver, ReadyToUse true and a snapshot handle. Requested capacity must cover restoreSize when present; enabled mode-conversion protection checks the snapshot-content permission annotation.

SMB v1.20.0 rejects Block capability. Its snapshot RPCs are Unimplemented and its content-copy route rejects a snapshot source; a valid PVC snapshot reference cannot establish snapshot restore on SMB. Its PVC-clone route copies from the source SMB volume. Copy, SMB access and application consistency are separate from core binding.

On the selected SMB clone route, copyFromVolume parses the source handle, uses the first requested capability when present, and mounts source and destination through NodeStageVolume with the same CreateVolume secrets. An invalid source handle returns NotFound; either mount can fail. It then runs external cp -a from the source directory contents to the destination. Copy failure returns Internal with command output and does not undo a partially written destination. The command is not bound to RPC context cancellation, and deferred unmount errors only log warnings. Preserve both handles and inspect destination contents/mounts after a timeout or error; do not replay or delete the destination as if no copy occurred. This route does not quiesce the source application or verify an independently restored reader.

After Bound/PV UID checks, CSI attach/mount is another receiving route. CSIDriver attachRequired:false skips attach; otherwise the controller creates/observes VolumeAttachment and Kubelet checks attachment. NodeStage runs only if the driver advertises STAGE_UNSTAGE_VOLUME; NodePublish receives read-only intent, mode, mount options and secrets. An RPC error can be uncertain, and an error after successful publication can leave the volume mounted.

SMB v1.20.0 NodeStage requires handle, capability, staging target and a source in volume context. It reads source/subDir and claim/PV metadata substitutions, uses a lock keyed by handle plus staging target, and resolves credentials from case-insensitive secret keys with trimmed username/password/domain. Guest mount options bypass username/password options. Persistent staging uses the supplied node-stage secrets; the separately identified ephemeral branch can fetch its configured Secret. Linux can use a Kerberos cache, create the staging directory and add the requested mount group when no gid flag is present; Windows uses its domain/username option path. Credential/cache/directory errors can stop before mounting and can leave local preparation artifacts.

SMB checks the actual staging mount point before work. An already-mounted readable target skips a new SMB mount. An unreadable existing target can be unmounted and still return its read error; inspect the actual target before retry. For a new mount it substitutes subDir metadata and calls Mount with the source, options and sensitive credentials through a 110-second WaitUntilTimeout wrapper. That wrapper returns the mount error or timeout without cancelling its mount goroutine. Inference from that wrapper and the deferred staging-lock release: timeout can leave mount work running after this call releases its lock. A failed staging response is not proof that the share is unmounted; retain handle/target and investigate current mounts and driver work before repeating it.

For SMB v1.20.0, persistent NodePublish binds the staging path to the container target, adding ro when requested. It can return success for an already-mounted target. Access to the actual SMB share, credentials, server data and application read/write checks remain necessary; Bound or successful mount is not a backup/restore proof.
